signals.topic: OpenRouterResponses injects additionalProperties:false causing xAI/Grok HTTP 400 on structured output
signals.summary: OpenRouterResponses inherits from OpenAIResponses which unconditionally sanitizes schemas with additionalProperties:false. xAI/Grok rejects this schema property with HTTP 400. Setting strict_output=False does not prevent this injection. Structured output is blocked for all non-OpenAI providers routed through OpenRouter.
aliases: OpenRouter structured output blocked for non-OpenAI providers
OpenRouterResponses schema sanitization incompatible with xAI
signals.review_reason: Structured output is completely broken for xAI/Grok via OpenRouter — every structured-output request fails with HTTP 400. Provider-aware schema injection is a real API incompatibility affecting a major provider.

source_issues.title: [Bug] OpenRouterResponses injects additionalProperties: false into schemas for non-OpenAI providers (xAI/Grok rejects with 400)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed HTTP 400 from xAI/Grok: 'Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/properties/additionalProperties: property schema false is not supported'. Root cause spans three injection paths: sanitize_response_schema() hardcodes 'openai' provider, parse_tools() sets strict=True triggering additionalProperties:false, and get_json_schema_for_arg() injects it regardless of strict mode. strict_output=False does not help.

signals.topic: RemoteDb route handlers crash with AttributeError when sort_order parameter is omitted
signals.summary: Four AgentOS routers declare sort_order as Optional[SortOrder] but default it to raw string 'desc' instead of SortOrder.DESC. On FastAPI 0.109.2, the raw string reaches the handler as str, then .value is called on it causing AttributeError. Affects /sessions, /evals, /memory, and /knowledge/content endpoints.
signals.review_reason: Direct AttributeError crash on multiple API routes (sessions, evals, memory, knowledge) triggered by omitting a single query parameter. Breaks AgentOS routers in FastAPI 0.109.2+ environments — a real service disruption.

source_issues.title: [Bug] RemoteDb routes define sort_order with a raw string default instead of SortOrder.DESC
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed crash: Four routers (session, evals, memory, knowledge) pass raw string default 'desc' for Optional[SortOrder] parameter. On FastAPI 0.109.2, the route handler receives str instead of SortOrder enum. RemoteDb branch executes 'sort_order.value' on a string, raising 'AttributeError: str object has no attribute value'. All four /sessions, /evals, /memory, /knowledge/content endpoints affected when RemoteDb path is used and sort_order is omitted.

signals.topic: Session compression silently discards user explicit instructions, causing assistant to write code without permission
signals.summary: After session compression, the assistant ignores user rules that explicitly prohibit code writing without permission, causing unintended code changes.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct users explicitly prohibit code changes; after session compression the rules are silently dropped and the assistant writes code anyway. Violates user intent and trust in a critical workflow (code modification). count=2 with matching titles confirms this is a recurring regression, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Assistant continues coding after session compression
source_issues.evidence: User set explicit rule 'Kein Code schreiben ohne explizite Erlaubnis' (no code without permission). After session compression the assistant writes code without permission; original rules appear lost after compression.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Assistant continues coding after session compression despite explicit prohibition
source_issues.evidence: User set explicit rules 'Do not write any code without explicit permission' and 'Discuss first, then code once go-ahead is given'. After compression, assistant begins writing code without permission.

signals.topic: Built-in MCP servers (chrome-devtools, morphllm-fast-apply) cannot be disabled, wasting tokens and expanding attack surface
signals.summary: chrome-devtools and morphllm-fast-apply are hardcoded in the binary and spawned on every session with no configuration mechanism to disable them, consuming context tokens and launching browser/npm processes.
signals.review_reason: count=2 duplicate reports with rich evidence. Users forced to pay token overhead for chrome-devtools and morphllm-fast-apply on every session. chrome-devtools launches browser process; morphllm-fast-apply executes remote npm code. Users cannot reduce attack surface or optimize context window. Though labeled FEATURE, the inability to opt out creates measurable cost and security impact.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE]: Allow disabling built-in MCP servers (chrome-devtools, morphllm-fast-apply)
source_issues.evidence: chrome-devtools and morphllm-fast-apply are spawned on every session startup even when opencode.json contains no reference to them. Binary contains hardcoded npm exec commands. Attempting to configure enabled:false causes fatal validation error. Both servers originate from the binary, not user config.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE]: Allow disabling built-in MCP servers (chrome-devtools, morphllm-fast-apply)
source_issues.evidence: count=2 duplicate reports from same author providing additional evidence: chrome-devtools launches browser process, morphllm-fast-apply executes remote npm code. Token overhead on every session; config hygiene broken; public schema does not declare mcp field. Users cannot reduce attack surface.

signals.topic: SSE connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT cause unbounded AsyncQueue memory growth (~14 MB/sec), making Desktop unusable over time
signals.summary: Memory leak from zombie SSE connections in CLOSE_WAIT state causes unbounded RAM growth at 14 MB/sec; sessions become unresponsive after sustained use.
signals.review_reason: Unbounded memory leak causing 24.5 GB peak RAM. Main flow failure: OpenCode Desktop becomes progressively more unresponsive until unusable. Concrete measurements with 66-74 zombie connections; not theoretical. Affects all users with intermittent connections or window minimize/restore cycles.

source_issues.title: Memory leak: SSE connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT cause unbounded AsyncQueue growth (~14 MB/sec)
source_issues.evidence: Memory grows +434 MB in 30 seconds (14.5 MB/sec) with stable zombie connection count. Peak observed: 24.5 GB RAM. Root cause: onAbort never called when TCP enters CLOSE_WAIT in Bun/Hono. AsyncQueue in src/util/queue.ts has no size limit and no backpressure.

signals.topic: auth login fetches remote config and executes returned auth.command without user confirmation (arbitrary code execution)
signals.summary: opencode auth login silently fetches remote .well-known/opencode and immediately runs the returned auth.command, enabling arbitrary command execution by a malicious server.
signals.review_reason: Arbitrary code execution during auth flow with zero user confirmation. A malicious or compromised .well-known server can make opencode execute any command on the user's machine. Clear user impact: data loss or system compromise risk, not theoretical security concern.

source_issues.title: auth login <url> should confirm before running auth.command
source_issues.evidence: opencode auth login fetches remote .well-known/opencode and immediately runs returned auth.command. A remotely provided command like 'touch /tmp/oc-bug' executes without any user approval or confirmation dialog.

signals.topic: Subagent calling a forbidden tool causes session to hang forever with no recovery
signals.summary: When a subagent calls a tool configured with 'ask' permission, the entire session hangs permanently instead of handling the denial gracefully.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blockage when using opencode run with subagents: entire session permanently hangs with no timeout or recovery mechanism. Users must kill the process and lose work. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact evidence sufficient for P0 per the rules.

source_issues.title: If subagent runs a forbidden tool call, session hangs forever.
source_issues.evidence: When agent calls a sub-agent and the sub-agent tries to call a forbidden tool, the session hangs forever. No timeout, no error, no recovery. User must kill the process. Reproducible with opencode run and permission configuration.

signals.topic: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() and WebSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() omitzero drops required fields causing 400 API errors
signals.summary: ToParam() serialization helpers use omitzero tag on required fields; when the field value is the zero value (e.g., empty string), the field is dropped entirely, causing the API to reject the next request with 'Field required' 400 error. This breaks multi-turn agentic loops and beta sessions flows.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issue reports (#317, #242) confirm the same root cause: omitzero tag on required fields in ToParam() serialization helpers causes field drop. This directly breaks the main agentic loop workflow: when the API returns an error condition, the next API call fails with 400 because a required field is missing. This is a main-flow-blocking bug for users using tool search or web search in multi-turn conversations.

source_issues.title: ToolSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field via omitzero
source_issues.evidence: omitzero tag on ErrorCode causes the field to be dropped when value is zero/empty. Next API call returns 400: 'messages.14.content.1.tool_search_tool_result.content.RequestToolSearchToolResultError.error_code: Field required'. Breaks multi-turn agentic-loop conversations. Confirmed in v1.35.0 and v1.34.0. Related to #242 same bug class with WebSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam().

source_issues.title: BetaWebSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops required error_code field via omitzero
source_issues.evidence: Same omitzero bug class affecting WebSearchToolResultBlock.ToParam(). error_code field dropped when zero value. Linked as same root cause from #317.

signals.topic: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper omits required Type field causing 400 on sessions events API
signals.summary: The helper function BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage() does not set the required Type field on BetaManagedAgentsUserMessageEventParams, causing all calls to POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events to fail with 400 'events[0].type: Field required'. The beta managed agents user message feature is completely non-functional when using this helper.
aliases: beta managed agents user message helper bug
signals.review_reason: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage is a public helper function that is entirely broken — it produces structs missing the required Type field, making every call to the sessions events API fail with 400. While only one issue report, the user impact is severe: the beta managed agents user message feature is completely unusable through this helper, which is the intended API entry point.

source_issues.title: BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage helper omits required Type field
source_issues.evidence: Helper function BetaManagedAgentsEventParamsOfUserMessage() sets Content but never sets Type on BetaManagedAgentsUserMessageEventParams. Calling POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events with this helper returns 400 Bad Request: 'events[0].type: Field required'. The feature is entirely non-functional through the SDK helper. All other similar helpers in the same file correctly accept and set their type parameter.

signals.topic: Streaming: JSON marshal error when stopping mid tool-call due to max token limit
signals.summary: During streaming responses, when the model hits the max_tokens limit in the middle of a tool call, the SDK throws 'json: error calling MarshalJSON for type json.RawMessage: unexpected end of JSON input'. This causes streaming to fail non-gracefully, breaking the user experience for any tool-calling workflow near token limits.
aliases: streaming JSON marshal error token limit
unexpected end of JSON input streaming
signals.review_reason: Streaming is a primary workflow path for the SDK. When the model hits max_tokens mid tool-call, the SDK panics/errors with a JSON marshal error, completely breaking the streaming response for that turn. This affects any user using streaming with tool calls near token boundaries. Reported in a labeled SDK issue with clear reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: Streaming: json: error calling MarshalJSON for type json.RawMessage: unexpected end of JSON input
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in v1.26.0. Streaming fails with 'unexpected end of JSON input' when the model stops mid tool-call due to max_tokens limit. User's tool-calling workflow is broken when approaching token limits. This is a reproducible runtime failure of the streaming code path.

signals.topic: Structured Output: Java nullable/Optional fields are incorrectly marked as required in JSON Schema, causing LLM hallucination
signals.summary: When using StructuredMessageCreateParams with Java classes, all fields (including nullable and Optional fields) are added to the `required` array of the generated JSON Schema. This forces LLMs to hallucinate placeholder values (e.g. "null", empty string) for fields that should be optional, degrading output quality and correctness of structured data extraction.
aliases: Structured output Java nullable fields treated as required
Java reflection schema generation ignores @Nullable and Optional types
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point with concrete evidence: the issue describes a production use case (court document analysis with LlmVerdictOutput record) where the SDK's schema generator forces all Java fields into the JSON Schema `required` array regardless of nullability annotations or Optional types. The consequence is direct — LLMs generate hallucinated placeholder values (null strings, empty strings, dashes) for fields that should be omitted, corrupting structured output data. This is not a feature request; it is a correctness defect that breaks the primary structured output workflow for Java SDK users.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional all fail to mark fields as optional in the generated JSON Schema. Every field lands in the `required` array, causing the LLM (Claude 3.5/4.5) to hallucinate values to satisfy schema constraints even when system prompts instruct the LLM to leave fields empty.

signals.topic: Prompt caching fails silently in streaming mode (client.beta.messages.stream)
signals.summary: When using streaming mode (beta.messages.stream), prompt caching metadata (cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens) is never returned, causing caching to be completely non-functional in streaming requests. Users lose the cost-reduction benefits of prompt caching in any streaming workflow.
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues confirm the same root: prompt caching is broken in streaming mode. In #1343 streaming always produces zero cache tokens vs HTTP which works. In #1349, skills cause non-deterministic cache prefix in streaming, leading to zero cache reads on repeated requests. This directly causes financial loss (lost cache savings) for any user running streaming workloads with custom skills or prompt caching. Both are open/unresolved.

source_issues.title: Caching does not work or not return cache info when streaming is enabled
source_issues.evidence: HTTP mode shows cache_read/cache_write tokens; streaming mode shows zero cache tokens in the same SDK call path. Confirmed by user with screenshots comparing HTTP vs streaming response metadata.

source_issues.title: Custom skills in container parameter break prompt caching - consistent skills list produces non-deterministic cache prefix
source_issues.evidence: cache_read_input_tokens=0 on Turn 2 with skills present when it should read ~37097 tokens. With skills absent, cache hits correctly. Turn 2 shows read=33852 at system+tools level but write=3448 on messages, confirming non-deterministic cache prefix when custom skills are involved.

signals.topic: Managed Agents streaming (client.beta.sessions.events.stream) silently drops all events
signals.summary: The Stream class in anthropic/_streaming.py is hardcoded to only handle Messages API event types. All managed agents SSE event types (session.status_*, agent.message, agent.tool_use, agent.thinking, span.model_request_*, etc.) are not matched in the if-chain and are silently dropped. Any user calling client.beta.sessions.events.stream() receives zero events.
signals.review_reason: Core managed agents streaming feature is completely non-functional in SDK 0.93.0. The bug is precisely located in Stream.__stream__() with a self-contained repro proving 0/3 events delivered. This blocks the primary use case of managed agents (real-time event streaming) for all users. High severity due to complete feature failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Managed Agents: client.beta.sessions.events.stream() silently drops all events
source_issues.evidence: User provided minimal repro (no server required) proving Stream.__stream__ yields 0 events out of 3 sent managed agents SSE events. The Stream class if-chain only handles Messages API event names; all managed agents event types fall through with no else clause. Impact: 'every consumer of client.beta.sessions.events.stream() is affected — managed agents streaming is entirely broken in 0.93.0.'

signals.topic: web_search dynamic filtering causes excessive pause_turn failures (~55-60%) in batch production workflows, wasting API costs
signals.summary: The web_search_20250209 tool's internal dynamic filtering code_execution loop hits the 10-iteration server limit and returns pause_turn with ~110 content blocks, producing no usable output. Occurs on 55-60% of batch requests, causing batch jobs to run 9+ hours with only 50-60% completion rate. Failed attempts still incur full token costs. Workaround (allowed_callers: ['direct']) is undocumented.
aliases: web search pause_turn high failure rate
signals.review_reason: While the root cause of the dynamic filtering loop is partly server-side model behavior, the SDK is the user-facing interface for this tool and the production impact is severe: 55-60% failure rate in automated batch workflows with direct cost waste per failed request. The undocumented allowed_callers workaround is the actionable fix accessible through the SDK API. This constitutes a significant reliability and cost-loss pain point for production users.

source_issues.title: `web_search_20250209` dynamic filtering causes excessive `pause_turn` at ~110 content blocks — batch processing impractical
source_issues.evidence: Production batch statistics: 55-60% pause_turn rate across 50+ requests, 100% success with allowed_callers workaround, batch time drops from 9+ hours to 38 minutes. Cost per failed attempt ~$0.15-0.25 (tokens consumed but no output). User provides full side-by-side comparison table proving workaround effectiveness.

signals.topic: BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool docstring is copy-pasted from sync class, causes TypeError when users follow docs
signals.summary: The async memory tool class docstring uses the synchronous base class (BetaAbstractMemoryTool), synchronous method signatures (def instead of async def), and sync client (Anthropic instead of AsyncAnthropic). Users who follow the documentation verbatim get TypeError at instantiation. The sync counterpart docstring is correct.
signals.review_reason: Documentation error causes TypeError at instantiation when users follow the official docstring example for the async memory tool class. This is a developer experience regression — the async class docstring was clearly copy-pasted from the sync class without updates. Though single-incident, it directly blocks correct usage of a documented API and wastes developer time debugging a non-intuitive error.

source_issues.title: BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool docstring contains sync-only example (copy-paste from sync class)
source_issues.evidence: Three specific docstring errors: (1) wrong base class BetaAbstractMemoryTool instead of BetaAsyncAbstractMemoryTool, (2) sync def instead of async def for view/create methods, (3) Anthropic() instead of AsyncAnthropic() client. User identifies the sync counterpart docstring is correct, proving this is a copy-paste error.

signals.topic: SDK module import time of ~209ms causes 300ms+ import overhead for downstream packages
signals.summary: Importing any single type from the anthropic package costs ~209ms. This is caused by the package importing all submodules (anthropic.lib.tools, anthropic.types) eagerly on import, even when only one type is needed. Downstream packages like langchain_anthropic take 300ms+ just to import due to this, destroying latency-sensitive application performance.
signals.review_reason: 209ms import time is a measurable performance regression for any application that uses anthropic as a dependency. For latency-sensitive applications (API servers, serverless functions, CLI tools), this adds hundreds of milliseconds to cold start times. The issue explicitly shows downstream ecosystem impact on langchain_anthropic. This is a well-documented, reproducible performance degradation that affects all SDK users.

source_issues.title: Slow imports
source_issues.evidence: python3 -X importtime shows: anthropic.lib.tools takes 69ms, anthropic.types takes 116ms, total anthropic import is 209ms. Even importing a single specific type (image_block_param) still triggers full 208ms import of the parent package. langchain_anthropic downstream takes 300ms+ from import alone.

signals.topic: Streaming pipeline crashes with unhandled SyntaxError when model outputs invalid JSON escape sequences (e.g., regex-like \d/\s/\p, PHP namespaces, Windows paths)
signals.summary: MessageStream's JSON.parse calls throw unhandled SyntaxError when model emits strings with invalid JSON escape sequences, crashing the entire Node.js process. Two independent reporters hit this with different escape patterns (regex literals vs PHP namespaces).
aliases: JSON.parse crash on invalid escape sequences
partialParse crashes on invalid JSON escapes
streaming JSON parse error crashes process
signals.review_reason: Two independent users hit this bug with different invalid escape patterns (regex literals in #996 and PHP namespaces in #986). Both crash the streaming pipeline with unhandled SyntaxError, which is a Node.js process-level failure — the highest severity user impact. No workaround exists within the SDK. Confirmed reproducible on real model output.

source_issues.title: bug(streaming): JSON.parse crashes on invalid escape sequences in model output
source_issues.evidence: unhandled SyntaxError: Invalid escape sequence crashes Node.js process when model outputs strings with regex-like escape sequences (\d, \p, \s)

source_issues.title: partialParse in _vendor/partial-json-parser crashes on invalid JSON escape sequences from model output
source_issues.evidence: partialParse() throws 'Bad escaped character in JSON' when model emits PHP namespaces (App\Http\Middleware) in tool call JSON, killing the entire streaming response

signals.topic: O(N²) string concatenation in MessageStream text accumulation causes severe performance degradation for long streaming responses
signals.summary: MessageStream uses += string concatenation in a loop, which is O(N²) due to string immutability in JavaScript. Streaming 4K tokens takes ~16x longer than optimal; 10K tokens ~100x slower. Affects all users generating long structured outputs or code.
signals.review_reason: Single issue but backed by detailed benchmarks showing 16x-100x performance degradation on realistic workloads (4K-10K tokens). The root cause (string immutability + loop concatenation) is a well-understood JavaScript performance anti-pattern. All users generating long responses via streaming are impacted with no workaround. The performance delta is large enough to materially slow down production workloads.

source_issues.title: perf(MessageStream): O(N²) complexity in text accumulation during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: Benchmark demonstrates 4K tokens ~16x slower than linear; 10K tokens ~100x slower. Root cause identified as += string concatenation in MessageStream. No SDK-level workaround; all long-output users are affected.

signals.topic: ProcessError stderr/exit_code destroyed during exception propagation — CLI failures produce only generic 'Command failed with exit code 1' with hardcoded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
signals.summary: When the bundled CLI subprocess exits non-zero, the original ProcessError (with structured exit_code and stderr fields) is destroyed across query.py and subprocess_cli.py, re-raised as a bare Exception. Users cannot catch ProcessError, cannot access exit_code, and stderr contains a hard-coded literal string instead of actual subprocess output. This makes diagnosing CLI failures (bad model alias, permission denied, config errors) impossible without forking the SDK. Three issues (#800, #798) independently reported this exact root cause.
aliases: stderr hardcoded literal instead of actual output
ProcessError type destroyed into bare Exception
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：CLI 子进程失败（如无效模型别名、权限拒绝、配置错误）是常见场景，用户无法捕获 ProcessError、无法访问 exit_code、无法获得实际 stderr，所有诊断信息被三层代码全部抹除。2 个独立 issue 证实相同根因，且 issue #798 明确指出历史上已有 #515/#282/#238 等多次同类投诉。这是 SDK 错误处理的核心缺陷，完全阻断用户排查失败原因。

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: Triple defect: (1) subprocess_cli.py hardcodes stderr='Check stderr output for details', never capturing actual subprocess stderr; (2) query.py flattens ProcessError to str(e) in message reader, losing exit_code/stderr attrs; (3) receive_messages() raises bare Exception, not ClaudeSDKError or ProcessError. Verified repro with claude-haiku-4-5-20241022 (invalid model alias) — user gets no actionable stderr, no exit_code, cannot isinstance(exc, ProcessError).

source_issues.title: Error context destroyed through exception flattening — CLI failures produce unhelpful 'Command failed with exit code 1'
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause independently reported: stderr hardcoded literal, str(e) flattening destroys ProcessError, bare Exception re-raised. References closed issues #515, #282, #238 as prior hits by same problem. Lists specific lines in subprocess_cli.py and query.py causing the destruction chain.

signals.topic: setting_sources=[] silently ignored due to Python truthiness check — empty list treated as None, CLI falls back to loading all default sources including account-level MCP integrations
signals.summary: In subprocess_cli.py _build_command, the condition 'if self._options.setting_sources:' uses Python truthiness check. Since [] is falsy, passing setting_sources=[] never sends --setting-sources to CLI subprocess, which falls back to loading all default sources (user, project, local) including account-level claude.ai MCP integrations. This is a bug distinct from the same-pattern issue with allowed_tools (which was fixed in #634). Two independent issues (#802 closed, #794 open) reported this exact bug.
aliases: Python falsy empty list bug in _build_command
signals.review_reason: 非阻断性 bug 但影响明确：setting_sources=[] 本应禁用所有设置源（包括用户账户级别的 MCP 集成），但因 Python 列表真假值判断被静默忽略，用户无法阻止不需要的 MCP 工具被加载。2 个独立 issue 确认同一根因，虽 issue #802 已 closed，但 issue #794 表明问题仍存在，影响需要隔离环境的 SDK 用户。优先级 P2 因 count=2 但非主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] (empty list) silently ignored — global settings always loaded
source_issues.evidence: Bug confirmed: if self._options.setting_sources: branch never executes for []. SDK loads all setting sources instead. Issue closed but fix not merged in the data snapshot (issue #794 is open on same bug). Workaround: setting_sources=[''] forces the flag through truthiness check.

source_issues.title: setting_sources=[] silently ignored due to truthiness check in _build_command
source_issues.evidence: References similar bug #634 for allowed_tools which was fixed. setting_sources still uses truthiness check, making empty list indistinguishable from 'not set'. Provides comparison with tools handling that correctly uses 'is not None' check.

signals.topic: 429 rate limit crashes agent session — SDK raises fatal exception instead of backing off and retrying, destroying multi-turn autonomous sessions
signals.summary: SDK crashes fatally when API returns 429 rate limit error, treating a transient recoverable condition as fatal. Multi-turn autonomous agent sessions accumulating 10+ minutes of work are destroyed by a single rate limit hit, losing all progress. The SDK knows the rate limits and has access to Retry-After headers but does not use them. On a 30k tokens/minute rate limit, sessions reliably crash within 10-15 minutes, making the SDK unusable for autonomous multi-turn agents without manual intervention.
aliases: SDK should retry on 429 instead of crashing
429 treated as fatal instead of transient
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 + 成本损失：SDK 官方客户端对自家 API 的 429 限流直接抛致命异常而非退避重试，导致累积 10-20 轮的多轮自主 agent 会话被全部销毁。Issue 提供了具体成本数据（每次崩溃浪费约 2 美元）和确定性复现路径（读大文件超过每分钟 token 限额即崩溃），且明确说明 Retry-After header 存在但 SDK 未使用。这是 SDK 的核心职责缺失——SDK 控制着完整 agent 循环、工具执行和上下文压缩，限流处理是其天然职责的一部分。

source_issues.title: Agent SDK should handle 429 rate limits gracefully instead of crashing
source_issues.evidence: Explicit repro: agent reading 10-25KB files via MCP tools over 15-20 turns hits 429 after accumulated context exceeds 30k tokens/min. SDK raises fatal exception, entire session destroyed. Three runs in 2 hours, all crashed at same point with 80-90% work completed. Cost: ~2.5 USD wasted per crash vs 0.5 USD for successful run. Workaround (asyncio.sleep between turns) does not prevent crash because SDK raises exception internally before caller's try/except can intercept. Retry-After header exists but is not used.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() normal completion — asyncgen finalizer triggers cross-task cancel that pins CPU at 100% until process restart
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport in subprocess_cli.py uses anyio.create_task_group() with manual __aenter__/__aexit__ for stderr reading, the same anti-pattern fixed in PR #746 for query.py but not applied to this sibling file. Every normal completion of async for message in query(...) triggers cross-task cancel scope exit via asyncgen_athrow, which cancels the caller's task from an unrelated context and pins anyio's _deliver_cancellation in a 100% CPU loop. One stuck scope per completed agent — they accumulate until process restart. Deterministic, reproducible on every normal completion.
aliases: anyio task group cancel scope leak on asyncgen finalization
CPU 100% loop from asyncgen finalizer cross-task cancel
stderr task group leak same as #454/#776 but in subprocess_cli.py
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 + 体验严重下降：任何正常的 query() 完成都会触发此 bug，导致进程 CPU 100% 且持续到重启。由于每个 agent 完成都会累积一个 stuck scope，长期运行进程性能持续恶化。这是 asyncgen finalization 与 anyio task group 跨任务取消作用域的组合缺陷，影响所有使用 SubprocessCLITransport 的用户，且 issue 提供了完整的修复 diff 和已验证的修复方案。

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic on every normal query() completion. Verified with 4+ consecutive agent completions: before fix CPU stays at 100%+ until process restart, after fix CPU stays <15%. Captured tracebacks showing cross-task cancel via async_generator_athrow. References prior occurrences: #454 and #776 hit the same failure mode in query.py, PR #746 fixed query.py but missed the same pattern in subprocess_cli.py. Stuck scopes accumulate per completed agent.

signals.topic: continue_conversation=True does not resume previous session — new session_id created on every script run even when previous run fully completed
signals.summary: ClaudeAgentOptions(continue_conversation=True) does not resume the previous session after restarting the script. A new session_id is created on every run regardless of same script, same cwd, and previous run reaching ResultMessage. This is a documented feature that is completely broken — users cannot rely on the continue_conversation option for multi-session workflows.
aliases: session not resumed on script restart
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：continue_conversation 是文档明确记录的功能，用户依赖此选项实现多会话工作流，但完全失效——每次脚本重启都创建新 session 而非恢复上一个会话。这不是边缘场景，而是 SDK 的核心多会话管理功能。

source_issues.title: continue_conversation=True starts a new session instead of resuming the previous one
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro provided: run same script twice with continue_conversation=True, second run gets different session_id. According to docs, this option should continue the most recent session in the directory. Both runs use same script, same cwd, previous run fully completes to ResultMessage — yet session is not resumed.

signals.topic: Plugin initialization regression: control request timeout during SDK control protocol handshake (SDK 0.1.45+)
signals.summary: Plugin initialization fails with 'Control request timeout: initialize' in SDK versions 0.1.45 through 0.1.56. The hardcoded 65-second timeout in _send_control_request() is exceeded during the SDK's control protocol initialization phase, completely breaking plugin loading for all affected versions. Rolling back to 0.1.44 resolves it.
signals.review_reason: Plugin initialization is completely blocked across 12+ SDK versions (0.1.45-0.1.56). The SDK throws 'Control request timeout: initialize' and exits, making plugins entirely unusable for all consumers on those versions. This is a confirmed regression with a clear rollback workaround and full reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: Plugin initialization fails with "Control request timeout: initialize" error in claude-agent-sdk versions 0.1.45 and above
source_issues.evidence: SDK 0.1.45-0.1.56 all fail plugin initialization; hardcoded 65-second timeout exceeded; working in 0.1.44; provides full stack trace from _send_control_request()

signals.topic: outputFormat returns misleading 'subtype: success' with absent structured_output for non-trivial schemas
signals.summary: When using outputFormat with nested or complex JSON schemas, the SDK returns subtype: 'success' but structured_output is undefined, even though the model correctly produces the JSON in the result text. The SDK never returns error_max_structured_output_retries as it should. This misleads consumers into believing structured output was successfully validated when it was silently dropped.
signals.review_reason: This is a critical SDK contract violation: outputFormat is a core structured-output feature, but the SDK silently drops validated output for any schema beyond trivial complexity, returning 'success' with no structured_output and no error. Users cannot trust the SDK's output for real-world schemas. This breaks the primary value proposition of the feature.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries
source_issues.evidence: Comprehensive reproduction with simple vs nested schemas; provides test table showing all nested/deep schemas return undefined structured_output with success subtype; correct JSON exists in result text but SDK fails to extract; affects SDK 0.2.97 on Node.js v22 with multiple models.

signals.topic: Bun --compile build fails due to missing tempfile.js in published npm package (SDK 0.2.96 regression)
signals.summary: Upgrading from SDK 0.2.91 to 0.2.96 breaks Bun compiled builds because extractFromBunfs.js imports './tempfile.js', a file absent from the published npm artifact and missing from the package files list. The build fails immediately with 'Could not resolve: "./tempfile.js"'.
signals.review_reason: SDK publish process is shipping broken artifacts. This is a confirmed build regression: the published npm package contains a file that imports a non-existent module, breaking all consumers using Bun compiled builds. Clear reproduction steps, exact error, and confirmed regression window.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.2.96: bun --compile fails due to missing ./tempfile.js import target
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly identifies the regression window (0.2.91->0.2.96); exact error message; identifies tempfile.js as missing from both package contents and package files list; rolling back to 0.2.91 resolves.

signals.topic: Monitor tool not listed or loaded in SDK despite being specified in tool list and documented
signals.summary: Users specifying the Monitor tool in the SDK tool list do not see it in the SDK initialization log or tool list. The Monitor tool is listed in the Claude Code SDK docs as a built-in tool but does not appear at runtime, blocking users from testing it via the SDK.
aliases: Monitor tool not appearing in SDK tool list
signals.review_reason: A documented built-in tool is not loadable through the SDK, despite being listed in official SDK docs. This blocks users from using a key feature (Claude Code Monitor) via the SDK, which is the intended integration path.

source_issues.title: Monitor tool not loading in SDK
source_issues.evidence: User on latest SDK version specifies Monitor in tool list but it does not appear in init log; tool is documented in SDK docs as a built-in tool but does not load at runtime.

signals.topic: Skills fail to load when cwd and homedir are the same directory
signals.summary: Skills are not loaded from cwd/.claude/skills when the current working directory and home directory are identical, preventing skill-based functionality from working in certain environment configurations.
signals.review_reason: Skills are a core extensibility mechanism of the SDK. A specific path-configuration causes them to silently fail to load, making the entire skill system unavailable for affected users without any error message.

source_issues.title: Skills not loaded when cwd and homedir are the same
source_issues.evidence: Bug report explicitly states skills fail to load from cwd/.claude/skills when cwd equals homedir; this is a specific path-resolution edge case.

signals.topic: v1.0.90 breaks AWS Bedrock SigV4 authentication — all Bedrock workflows fail with 403
signals.summary: After v1.0.90 (SDK 0.2.96, CLI 2.1.96) was released, AWS Bedrock auth is broken. The SDK sends a bare base64 Authorization header instead of proper AWS SigV4 format, causing 403 errors for all Bedrock users.
aliases: AWS credentials not forwarded for Bedrock
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 + 高频：3条issue来自不同用户，确认v1.0.90升级后所有Bedrock工作流均失败。SDK发送的Authorization header为原始base64而非AWS SigV4格式，导致API返回403。用户被迫回退到v1.0.89作为临时方案。#1201进一步表明SDK 0.2.92在tag mode下因exitError检查导致validateHeaders立即崩溃，这是持续性问题（非已修复的regression）。

source_issues.title: Bedrock SigV4 authentication broken after v1.0.90 (Claude Code 2.1.96 / Agent SDK 0.2.96)
source_issues.evidence: Same workflow succeeded at 04:42 UTC (pre-update, v1.0.89) then failed at 04:59 UTC (post-update, v1.0.90). Authorization header sent as bare base64 instead of AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 format. Multiple workflow types affected. Workaround: pin to v1.0.89.

source_issues.title: v1.0.90 breaks Bedrock auth with OIDC-assumed AWS credentials
source_issues.evidence: Same workflow: succeeds on v1.0.89, fails on v1.0.90 every time with 403 SigV4 signing error. AWS env vars confirmed valid via sts get-caller-identity. Action v1.0.90 broke the AWS credential chain forwarding to Claude Code subprocess.

source_issues.title: Bedrock validateHeaders error in tag mode (issue_comment + @claude), agent mode works fine
source_issues.evidence: Tag mode (issue_comment event with @claude) consistently fails with validateHeaders error while agent mode (prompt input + issues event) succeeds with identical configuration. Same action version, same SDK, same AWS credentials — only mode differs. Root cause: SDK 0.2.92 exitError check in streamInput path causes immediate crash in tag mode.

signals.topic: Bun runtime crashes with 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' — blocks all Claude Code action runs
signals.summary: Bun 1.3.6 crashes on startup with an internal fd mismatch error before Claude makes any API call, causing action to exit code 1. Affects multiple runner images and all recent action versions including pinned SHA.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：2条issue确认Bun运行时在启动阶段因fd错误崩溃，Claude Code在发出任何API请求前即退出code 1，且该错误影响了ubuntu-22.04和ubuntu-24.04上的所有action版本。另一条#1206的401错误也由相同Bun错误触发后发生。这两条issue共同证明action完全无法运行，用户的主流程被完全阻断。

source_issues.title: Consistent Bun crash: 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' — Claude Code process exits with code 1
source_issues.evidence: Same action SHA (657fb7c9) succeeded at 22:22 UTC then crashed at 23:03 UTC on same runner image. Bun fd 4 mismatch causes Claude Code process to exit with code 1 before any API call. Tested across ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04 and action versions v1.0.89, v1.0.90, v1.0.92, pinned SHA — all crash identically.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Action won't run due to 'app token exchange' GitHub App installation token (HTTP 401 Unauthorized)
source_issues.evidence: Action fails to run with Bun fd mismatch error followed by 401 Unauthorized on GitHub App token exchange. Both errors cause action to exit code 1, blocking the main workflow entirely.

signals.topic: Action crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks (cpSync dereference regression)
signals.summary: Since v1.0.89, the action crashes during config restoration when any SENSITIVE_PATH entry is a symlink. cpSync's default dereference:false causes symlink recreation to fail with ENOENT.
signals.review_reason: 体验下降 + 阻断：用户仓库中CLAUDE.md等配置文件使用symlink是常见实践（如从AGENTS.md链接），action在此场景下直接崩溃退出code 1，PR工作流完全失败。这是v1.0.89引入的regression，影响使用symlink的开发者群体。

source_issues.title: cpSync crashes with ENOENT when sensitive paths are symlinks
source_issues.evidence: Action crashes with ENOENT when CLAUDE.md is a symlink (e.g. CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md). cpSync in restore-config.ts defaults to dereference:false so it tries to recreate symlink at .claude-pr/ instead of copying file contents, failing because parent dir doesn't exist. Regression introduced in PR #1174. Workaround: pin to v1.0.88.

signals.topic: GitHub token expiration causes 401 errors — long-running jobs lose all work
signals.summary: GitHub tokens expire after 1 hour in GitHub Actions. When token expires mid-job, all subsequent GitHub API calls (commit, PR creation, comment posting) fail with 401, and all progress is lost with no branch or commit created.
aliases: long job token expiration lost work
signals.review_reason: 成本损失 + 主流程失败：token过期后Claude已完成的工作全部丢失（无branch、无commit、无comment）。用户等待超过1小时的CI job结果完全丢失，这是明显的成本损失和关键功能失效（commit/PR创建不可用）。action未在token过期前刷新token或保存checkpoint。

source_issues.title: 401 GitHub after 1 hour job, no branch no commits, no comment update
source_issues.evidence: Long-running job (>1 hour) completes Claude work but all GitHub API calls fail with 401 Bad credentials after token expires. Branch was never created, no commits made, no comment posted. All progress lost. Error shows octokit fails on GET /repos/.../issues/comments/... with HttpError Bad credentials. Also shows same Bun fd mismatch error as secondary symptom.

signals.topic: .husky added to SENSITIVE_PATHS breaks pre-commit hooks — regression from PR #1174
signals.summary: PR #1174 added .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS, causing the action to restore/reset the .husky directory during PR flows. This breaks repos that commit .husky files but rely on npx husky to install hooks, wiping pre-commit setup.
aliases: pre-commit hooks wiped after action runs
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：pre-commit hooks是开发者高频使用的质量门禁。action运行后hooks被静默清除，用户不会立即察觉，导致代码质量把关失效。这影响依赖git hooks进行lint/format/测试检查的开发团队。虽为单issue但影响范围广（.husky是npm生态常见模式）。

source_issues.title: Adding .husky to SENSITIVE_PATHS breaks repos that commit .husky files but not the hook setup
source_issues.evidence: After PR #1174, .husky directory is restored/reset during action run. Repos that commit .husky files (common pattern for preserving hook scripts) have their hook setup wiped — npx husky must be re-run to reinstall hooks. This is a regression from previous behavior where .husky was not treated as sensitive.

signals.topic: Claude Code executes irreversible blockchain token transfers without user confirmation, causing permanent financial loss
signals.summary: Claude Code executed an irreversible ERC20 transfer to a smart contract address without user confirmation, resulting in $99.88 USDC permanently stuck with no recovery method. The agent guessed the wrong deposit mechanism (Polymarket uses allowance-based CLOB, not a direct token transfer deposit step), and no confirmation prompt or small-amount test was performed before the irreversible on-chain transaction.
aliases: unconfirmed crypto transaction leading to fund loss
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: real financial loss ($99.88 USDC permanently unrecoverable) caused by Claude Code executing an irreversible blockchain transaction without user confirmation. The loss is verifiable on-chain. The core user harm is not 'security vulnerability' in the abstract — it is a specific workflow failure where the agent bypassed user consent for a high-risk financial operation, and the outcome was irreversible monetary damage. The lack of a confirmation gate before on-chain token transfers represents a systemic UX/safety gap that directly harms users who engage Claude Code with cryptocurrency tasks. Count=1 from one repo prevents P0, but the concrete financial harm and irreversibility of the outcome warrant P1 and keep=true.

source_issues.title: SAFETY: Claude Code lost user's .88 by blindly transferring USDC to a smart contract
source_issues.evidence: Real financial loss of $99.88 USDC confirmed via on-chain TX 0xce9d7593288161cd443beb7c2cb3cb7395916628ce1e091a9391e35acff644af on Polygon. Funds permanently stuck in contract 0x4bFb41d5B3570DeFd03C39a9A4D8dE6Bd8B8982E with no recovery path. Agent acted without understanding the correct Polymarket deposit mechanism.

signals.topic: New Claude Code sessions fail to hit full prompt cache, burning tokens on every relaunch
signals.summary: Claude Code session relaunch/cache behavior is broken: skills and project/CLAUDE.md are not cached between sessions, causing up to 6505 cache-create tokens consumed per new session even for identical prompts seconds apart. Root causes include git status output in system prompt (prevents caching) and git instructions in ephemeral system blocks.
aliases: Skills and CLAUDE.md not cached between sessions
git status in system prompt prevents prompt caching
signals.review_reason: User-impacting: every new Claude Code session burns thousands of cache-create tokens on costs with no user benefit. Two independent issues confirm the same root cause (git status in system prompt, skills/CLAUDE.md not cached). Causes direct financial loss via excessive token consumption across every session relaunch.

source_issues.title: [BUG] new sessions will **never** hit a (full)cache
source_issues.evidence: Relaunching claude / clearing the session costs 6505 cache-create tokens even after seconds and super short messages. Skills and project/CLAUDE.md not cached. Traffic inspection shows system prompts with <system-reminder> skills + memory + project/CLAUDE.md sent as user messages without cache_control.

source_issues.title: [BUG] uncachable system prompt caused by includeGitInstructions / CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS -> `git status`
source_issues.evidence: System prompt contains `git status` output in an ephemeral cache_control block, making every session unique and preventing cache hits. Observed: 11k cache read + 6k cache write on each relaunch vs 18k cache read when no changes.

signals.topic: AskUserQuestion auto-completes with empty answers under bypassPermissions + Skill context (v2.1.104 regression)
signals.summary: In v2.1.104, AskUserQuestion returns immediately with empty answers (`User has answered your questions: .`) without showing the interactive UI when invoked from within a Skill/command under bypassPermissions mode. Blocks all interactive slash command workflows. Regression from v2.1.101.
aliases: AskUserQuestion silent empty completion in skills
bypassPermissions causes AskUserQuestion to skip user input
signals.review_reason: Same-day regression from v2.1.104 actively blocking interactive slash command workflows (requirements elicitation, configuration, decision capture). Has multiple linked historical recurrences (#29547, #29733, #10400, #13439) confirming this is a persistent regression pattern. Model fabricating responses from empty answers is a critical trust/accuracy issue.

source_issues.title: AskUserQuestion auto-completes with empty answers in v2.1.104 (regression from v2.1.101)
source_issues.evidence: Regression in v2.1.104 (same day as file date). AskUserQuestion silently returns empty answers without showing UI under bypassPermissions + Skill context. Model proceeds with fabricated assumptions. Related historical issues #29547, #29733, #10400, #13439 confirm recurring pattern. Downgrade to v2.1.101 is the only workaround.

signals.topic: Opus 4.6 consumes excessive usage credits on routine prompts — 16% of 5-hour limit from a single simple investigation
signals.summary: Users reporting catastrophic token consumption from Opus 4.6 on simple prompts, burning usage limits at an order of magnitude above expected. Example: single simple investigation of CLAUDE.md consumed 16% of a 5-hour usage limit. Regression from v2.1.97.
aliases: Opus 4.6 burning through usage limits unexpectedly
Excessive token consumption on simple prompts in Opus
signals.review_reason: Single issue with explicit regression evidence and clear financial impact: 16% of usage limit from one routine prompt means users will exhaust their allocation mid-session with no warning. The magnitude of overconsumption (routine task consuming hours of budget) is qualitatively different from normal caching inefficiencies.

source_issues.title: [BUG] 16% of 5-hour usage limit consumed by simple investigation prompt.
source_issues.evidence: Single simple investigation of CLAUDE.md using Opus 4.6 (200k context) consumed 16% of 5-hour usage limit with no subagents, MCP servers, or long context explaining the blowup. User states: 'at this rate I'll be out of tokens the second I actually do something more complex.' Confirmed regression from 2.1.97.

signals.topic: write_file tool silently strips execute permissions from existing executable files
signals.summary: Filesystem write_file resets file permissions to 644 on every write, removing the execute bit from existing executable scripts without any warning or error. Scripts appear correct but silently fail to run downstream, causing repeated debugging sessions.
aliases: Executable shell scripts silently become non-executable after write_file
signals.review_reason: Silent failure mode: script content is correct but it won't execute, and the user has no indication why. The specific example (claude wrapper symlink) shows it can block Claude Code itself from launching. Repeated debugging across multiple conversations confirms this is not an edge case.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Filesystem write_file tool does not preserve file permissions
source_issues.evidence: write_file resets permissions to 644 on every write, stripping execute bit. Real-world impact: user's claude-wrapper script (a symlink target) had +x stripped, causing the claude symlink to fail silently on next invocation. Caused repeated debugging sessions across multiple conversations. Silent failure mode is the critical issue.

signals.topic: Channel notification handler silently drops inbound messages after ~2–3 hours on Docker/Linux
signals.summary: Claude Code's notifications/claude/channel event handler stops surfacing inbound MCP messages after 2–3 hours in long-running Docker/Linux sessions. The MCP plugin remains alive and actively polling (confirmed via strace/ss), but Claude Code no longer processes notifications. Requires session restart every ~2 hours as workaround.
aliases: Telegram/inbound MCP notifications stop after 2-3h in Docker
MCP channel notification handler time-based degradation
signals.review_reason: Time-based degradation of a core session feature with a clear reproduction timeline. Plugin is confirmed alive (not a plugin crash), proving this is a Claude Code-side handler leak/timeout. Requires manual session restart as workaround — directly interrupts long-running workflow sessions.

source_issues.title: Channel notification handler stops surfacing inbound messages after ~2-3h (Docker/Linux)
source_issues.evidence: Telegram plugin confirmed alive via strace (8 write syscalls/5s) and ss (ESTABLISHED TCP connections). Outbound MCP tools work during stall. Bug reproduced: inbound messages silently dropped after 2-3h. Workaround: restart every ~2h. Related: #46744, #46016, #46356. Separate from plugin poll-loop crash (anthropics/claude-plugins-official#1377).

signals.topic: LLM grading example has substring-matching bug causing all answers to be graded as correct
signals.summary: The grade_completion function in the documentation uses 'correct' in grader_response.lower() which matches 'incorrect' as True, making the evaluation system completely unreliable — every submission scores 100% regardless of actual correctness.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine bug in a documented cookbook example that makes the LLM-based grading system produce incorrect results. The substring bug 'correct' in 'incorrect' causes every answer to be graded as correct, rendering the entire evaluation system unreliable. While only 1 issue is reported, the impact is severe — any user following the official documentation example will get false-positive grading results, silently corrupting their evaluation pipeline. This qualifies as a user pain point with significant quality/accuracy implications.

source_issues.title: [BUG] False positive in LLM-based grading example
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with exact reproduction steps: when grader outputs 'incorrect', the substring check 'correct' in 'incorrect' evaluates to True, causing 100% score even with wrong golden answers. The issue includes a full reproduction script and a suggested fix.

signals.topic: Financial damage caused by Claude Code agent errors during Kaggle competition
signals.summary: A Claude Code agent (Opus 4.6) ran up ~$38-45 USD in charges through repeated configuration errors during a Kaggle competition, causing financial loss to a Max subscriber.
signals.review_reason: This issue documents clear financial damage (~$38-45 USD actual loss) caused by Claude Code agent misbehavior. Even though it is cross-posted and count=1, the explicit monetary loss to a subscriber makes it a user pain point. It is classified as P2 because it is a single report, not a high-frequency pattern, but the financial impact is real and documented.

source_issues.title: [SUPPORT] Financial damage report - Claude Code agent errors cost ~$45 USD
source_issues.evidence: Cross-post from claude-code/issues/42329. A Max subscriber incurred ~$38-45 USD in charges due to Claude Code agent repeatedly making configuration errors during a Kaggle competition. Issue is flagged as a support escalation with financial damage.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin poll loop permanently exits on transient non-409 errors — inbound messages silently stop
signals.summary: The Telegram plugin's poll loop only retries 409 Conflict errors; any other transient error (connection timeout, TLS reset, DNS hiccup, HTTP 5xx) causes the catch block to return, permanently exiting the polling loop. The process stays alive (MCP stdin keeps event loop running), so outbound tools still work, but the bot becomes completely deaf to inbound messages. This is a critical inbound flow breakage with confirmed strace evidence (zero TCP sockets to Telegram API).
aliases: poll loop exits on non-409 errors
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Telegram 插件的入站消息接收是核心功能，轮询循环永久退出导致 bot 完全聋哑。3 条 issue 有 strace 证据、日志证据和根因分析，符合 P0 高频+主流程阻断+样例链接支撑。#1378 提供了 strace 证据证明进程存活但零网络活动；#1345 确认入站消息被消耗但未渲染；#1360 显示版本升级后入站随 cron 触发规律性死亡。

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): poll loop exits permanently on non-409 errors — root cause of 'inbound stops' reports
source_issues.evidence: strace shows zero syscalls, zero TCP sockets to api.telegram.org; process alive but idle; outbound tools work while inbound is dead; #1378 identified this as root cause for 'outbound works, inbound stops' reports

source_issues.title: telegram@0.0.4: inbound messages consumed by server but never rendered as <channel> tag in Claude Code session
source_issues.evidence: Telegram bot polls and consumes updates but messages never appear as <channel source='telegram'> user turns; outbound reply/react works; confirmed via getWebhookInfo that updates are consumed (queue empty) but not rendered

source_issues.title: telegram v0.0.5: stale-poller SIGTERM kills legitimate concurrent sessions (regression from #1075 fix)
source_issues.evidence: v0.0.5 upgrade causes interactive session's Telegram poller to be killed by cron-triggered second session; inbound messages accumulate silently; logs show 'replacing stale poller' every 3 hours matching cron cadence

signals.topic: Telegram v0.0.5 stale-poller reclaim aggressively kills legitimate concurrent sessions (regression)
signals.summary: The v0.0.5 bot.pid stale-poller reclaim logic is too aggressive: it sends SIGTERM to any process whose PID appears in bot.pid without distinguishing orphans from legitimate concurrent sessions. This reliably kills the Telegram poller of a running interactive session whenever a second session (e.g. cron-triggered) starts. This is a confirmed regression from v0.0.4.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+回归：v0.0.5 的 stale-poller 回收逻辑将合法并发会话误判为孤儿进程并杀死，导致交互会话的 Telegram 轮询被 cron 任务杀死。日志证据显示每次 cron 触发都有 'replacing stale poller'，且从 v0.0.4 升级后规律性出现，符合回归特征。#1363 进一步证明双加载场景下 SIGTERM 导致 MCP 管道断裂，完全阻断 Telegram 功能。

source_issues.title: telegram v0.0.5: stale-poller SIGTERM kills legitimate concurrent sessions (regression from #1075 fix)
source_issues.evidence: v0.0.5 treats live PID in bot.pid as orphan and SIGTERMs it; cron-triggered second session kills interactive session's poller; grepped 325 plugin logs: 'replacing stale poller' appears every 3 hours starting 2026-04-11 04:03 UTC matching cron cadence; confirmed regression from v0.0.4

source_issues.title: Telegram 0.0.5: bot.pid SIGTERM kills MCP pipe on dual-load — acquireLock is safer
source_issues.evidence: Dual-load scenario: second bun process reads bot.pid, finds first process, sends SIGTERM; first bun dies causing MCP pipe break; telegram completely stops working for that session; only recoverable via full session restart

signals.topic: security-guidance hook outputs plain text instead of JSON — breaks Claude Code hook system with validation errors
signals.summary: The security-guidance plugin's PreToolUse hook outputs plain text to stderr when blocking, but Claude Code's hook system expects JSON format output. This causes 'hook json output validation failed' error on every trigger, making the security reminder hook completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：security-guidance hook 是安全提醒的核心机制，输出格式错误导致每次触发都产生验证错误，整个 hook 体系无法正常工作。用户在任何包含 dangerouslySetInnerHTML/eval/.innerHTML 的文件编辑时都会遇到此错误。

source_issues.title: security-guidance hook outputs plain text instead of JSON, causing 'json output validation' error
source_issues.evidence: security_reminder_hook.py line 272 uses print(reminder, file=sys.stderr) then sys.exit(2), outputting plain text; Claude Code hook system expects JSON format; every trigger produces 'hook json output validation failed' error

signals.topic: Marketplace schema validation errors block installation of all 15 affected plugins and entire marketplace add command
signals.summary: The marketplace.json file contains inconsistent source field formats across 15 plugins — some use object format (required) while others use string paths. Claude Code's schema validation fails on the entire marketplace add command, preventing all plugins from being installed.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：marketplace.json schema 验证错误导致 /plugin marketplace add 命令完全失败，15 个插件无法安装，且阻断整个插件市场功能。用户无法使用官方市场的任何插件。

source_issues.title: Schema validation errors in marketplace.json: 15 plugins have invalid source format
source_issues.evidence: /plugin marketplace add fails with schema validation errors for 15 plugins; source field uses string paths './plugins/...' instead of required object format; all 33+ plugins become unavailable even though only 15 have schema issues

signals.topic: Ralph Loop stop-hook blocks ALL project sessions when state file has empty session_id — causes infinite loop
signals.summary: The Ralph Loop stop-hook exits with block instead of skipping when the state file has an empty session_id. This causes ALL sessions in the project to enter an infinite loop: user's response triggers Stop, hook reads empty state, blocks all sessions, feeds loop prompt back, Claude responds, Stop fires again. Tokens burn continuously until user manually deletes the state file.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+明显成本损失：空 session_id 导致所有项目会话进入无限循环，持续消耗 tokens 直到手动删除状态文件。已有用户报告运行了约 48 次迭代才被发现，每次迭代都消耗 tokens，影响严重。

source_issues.title: Ralph Loop stop-hook blocks ALL sessions when session_id is empty
source_issues.evidence: Guard logic only skips when STATE_SESSION is non-empty AND differs from HOOK_SESSION; empty session_id causes guard to fall through and block every session; ran ~48 iterations across multiple sessions before being caught; tokens burned continuously until manual deletion of .claude/ralph-loop.local.md

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails to detect Git Bash despite correctly configured CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH on Windows

The bug is well-evidenced with detailed environment logs showing the env var is set at both levels, bash.exe is in PATH, and Git Bash works in the VS Code terminal — yet the extension fails to detect it. signals.topic: Delegated agents fail when using model/provider 'inherit' due to literal string passthrough
signals.summary: When an agent source uses model: inherit or provider: inherit in frontmatter, Goose passes the literal string 'inherit' to subagent resolution instead of inheriting the parent session config, causing 404 'model inherit not found' errors.
aliases: Delegate agent inherit model not working
model inherit passed as literal string to subagent
signals.review_reason: The delegate/subagent feature is completely broken when using the documented 'inherit' pattern — Goose passes the literal string 'inherit' instead of resolving to the parent session config, causing all delegated runs to fail with 404 errors. This is a primary feature (delegated agents) failure affecting the multi-agent workflow.

source_issues.title: Delegated agents treat `inherit` as a literal provider/model instead of inheriting parent session config
source_issues.evidence: Delegated agent runs fail with 'Request failed: Resource not found (404): model inherit not found' when agent frontmatter uses model: inherit. Fix validated in summon.rs. Affects any provider since inherit is forwarded literally.

signals.topic: act() fails with Anthropic models — response wrapped in $PARAMETER_NAME key causes AI_NoObjectGeneratedError
signals.summary: When using Anthropic models (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-5) as the default model for act(), the LLM response is wrapped in a $PARAMETER_NAME key. Zod schema validation then fails because all required fields are undefined at the top level, throwing AI_NoObjectGeneratedError. This blocks the primary act() workflow for all Anthropic users.
aliases: Anthropic model act() Zod validation failure
$PARAMETER_NAME wrapper breaks act() with Claude models
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: act() is a primary workflow in Stagehand and it completely breaks for all Anthropic model users. The error is reproducible and blocks the main extraction/action flow. The root cause is clear — Claude wraps tool output in a $PARAMETER_NAME key that Stagehand's response parser doesn't handle for Anthropic providers.

source_issues.title: act() fails with Anthropic models: response wrapped in $PARAMETER_NAME key
source_issues.evidence: act() throws AI_NoObjectGeneratedError when using Anthropic models because Zod validation fails — required fields elementId, description, method, arguments, twoStep are all undefined at top level. Reproducer provided with claude-sonnet-4-5. Issue does NOT occur with OpenAI models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1-mini). Root cause: Claude's tool_use response wraps output in the tool parameter name; Stagehand's parsing does not unwrap it for Anthropic models.

signals.topic: OpenAI reasoningEffort set to invalid value 'minimal' for gpt-5.4 — extract() throws AI_APICallError
signals.summary: Stagehand hardcodes reasoningEffort to 'minimal' for OpenAI models, but gpt-5.4 does not support this value (supported: 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh'). This causes extract() to throw AI_APICallError and fail, blocking the primary extract() workflow for gpt-5.4 users.
aliases: extract() broken with gpt-5.4 due to invalid reasoningEffort
signals.review_reason: Real user pain point: extract() is a core Stagehand workflow and it completely fails with gpt-5.4, producing an API-level error. The user provided a full minimal repro and identified the root cause in source code. The issue blocks the primary data extraction use case for gpt-5.4 users. Note: issue was later closed as fixed, but it represents a real period of user impact.

source_issues.title: Stagehand sets invalid OpenAI reasoningEffort: "minimal" for gpt-5.4
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproducible example provided. Stagehand calls OpenAI /v1/responses with reasoningEffort='minimal', which gpt-5.4 does not support, resulting in AI_APICallError. Root cause located at aisdk.ts#L183-L194. Proposed fix: change default from 'minimal' to 'low'. Issue closed as fixed on 2026-04-10.

signals.topic: keys tool does not perform variable substitution — %variableName% tokens typed literally
signals.summary: The keys tool (used by agents to simulate keyboard input) does not call substituteVariables() before typing, so %variableName% tokens are sent as literal strings instead of being resolved. This causes agents to type wrong values (e.g., literal '%token%' instead of the actual secret value). Variables are passed to other tools (type, act, fillForm) but not to keys.
aliases: variable substitution absent in keys tool
signals.review_reason: User pain point affecting agent workflows: when agents use the keys tool (a common pattern for clearing and replacing input field values), variable tokens are not substituted, causing wrong values to be typed. This breaks automation flows that rely on variable injection (e.g., typing credentials, tokens, or dynamic values). While not a main-flow blocker for all users, it is a significant and reproducible failure mode for agents using variable substitution with the keys tool.

source_issues.title: keys tool does not perform variable substitution
source_issues.evidence: When an agent uses the keys tool to clear an input field (Ctrl+A → Delete → type), the final type step via keys tool sends raw %token% literals instead of resolved values. Variables are correctly passed to typeTool but not to keysTool. Specific code locations identified: type.ts#L28 calls substituteVariables, but keys.ts#L33 sends raw value. Issue closed as fixed on 2026-04-09.

signals.topic: installV3ShadowPiercer ignores opts.debug — debug logging cannot be disabled
signals.summary: The V3ShadowPatchOptions interface defines a debug?: boolean option, but installV3ShadowPiercer hardcodes DEBUG = true and ignores the opts.debug parameter. This means debug console.info logs fire on every attachShadow call regardless of user preference, causing noise in logs and wasted console output.
aliases: shadow DOM piercer debug option ignored
debug logging always on in shadow piercer
signals.review_reason: User experience degradation: the debug option is part of the public API (V3ShadowPatchOptions) but is completely non-functional. This causes unwanted console noise on every shadow DOM attachShadow operation and prevents users from suppressing debug output. While not flow-blocking, it is a clear API contract violation that affects developer experience for any user working with shadow DOM pages.

source_issues.title: installV3ShadowPiercer ignores opts.debug — debug logging always enabled
source_issues.evidence: The opts.debug field in V3ShadowPatchOptions is never used; installV3ShadowPiercer hardcodes DEBUG = true with a comment acknowledging this ('hardcoded debug, remove later if desired'). Every attachShadow call triggers console.info('[v3-piercer] attachShadow', ...) regardless of user preference. Suggested fix: const DEBUG = opts.debug ?? false.

signals.topic: 并发Streaming场景下事件总线跨Run数据污染导致LLM输出流错乱
signals.summary: LLMStreamChunkEvent处理器注册在单例event bus上，并发运行时会将run A的chunk误发给run B的队列，导致输出内容跨Run混淆，用户无法获取正确的LLM流式输出。
aliases: singleton event bus chunk fan out
signals.review_reason: 并发streaming场景下LLM输出流被跨Run混淆是明确的体验下降问题。当用户同时运行多个crew实例时，event bus缺乏scope隔离会导致chunk被错误handler消费，输出结果不正确。这是关键功能的质量退化，虽然issue以feature-request形式提交，但作者已识别出具体的技术根因（单例event bus无run隔离）和明确的用户影响场景。

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Streaming handlers on singleton event bus can fan out chunks across concurrent runs
source_issues.evidence: issue作者明确指出并发streaming场景下，单例event bus缺少run/stream级别的scope隔离，run A发出的LLMStreamChunkEvent可能被run B的handler处理，导致chunk数据跨Run污染。这是流式输出场景下的数据正确性问题，高频并发使用时会触发。

signals.topic: WebSearchTool hardcoded HTTP timeout causes ReadTimeout errors in slow/corporate networks with no user override
signals.summary: WebSearchTool hardcodes timeout=30s across all search backends (google, bing, duckduckgo), and the Exa backend added in PR #2139 has no timeout at all. Users in corporate proxy environments or latency-sensitive applications cannot override this, leading to ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs mid-execution. No workaround exists without subclassing or monkey-patching.
aliases: hardcoded HTTP timeout ReadTimeout in search tools
signals.review_reason: Issue #2162 describes a concrete, reproducible workflow interruption: legitimate search requests fail with ReadTimeout in real network environments (corporate proxies, slow connections) with zero user-configurable workaround. This blocks agent execution mid-run and forces users to subclass or monkey-patch the tool. While count=1 limits it to P1 rather than P0, the blocking nature and lack of any override mechanism qualify it as a genuine user pain point.

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes two blocking scenarios: (1) corporate proxies/slow networks where legitimate requests exceed 30s causing avoidable ReadTimeout errors that abort agent runs; (2) latency-sensitive apps where 30s is too long. No user-configurable override exists, forcing subclassing or monkey-patching. Confirmed as regression risk from PR #2140 (security fixes) and PR #2139 (Exa backend).

Main-flow-blocking: users follow documented deploy workflow and their agent fails silently. No workaround other than manually adding dependencies.

signals.review_reason: SkillsMiddleware caching blocks the intended dynamic skill lifecycle — users cannot add or load new skills mid-session. This is a core use case for an agent framework (on-the-fly skill extension) being blocked by middleware caching behavior.

source_issues.title: The caching mechanism of SkillsMiddleware. After a skill is created, new skills cannot be dynamically uploaded and loaded based on the session.

Issue 36679 shows ONE malformed function dict drops ALL tool calls silently, completely breaking agent execution. Issue 36627 shows streaming deltas corrupt valid tool calls into blanks/invalid. Both affect the primary agent workflow with silent failures — users may not even know their tool calls were dropped.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud causing 2-3x redundant work and API cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls exceeding ~180 seconds are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while the original is still running. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, causing 2-3x duplicate LLM calls and API costs. Hardcoded heartbeat interval (BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120s) in langgraph-api appears to be the root cause.
aliases: duplicate tool calls on LangGraph Cloud
signals.review_reason: Causes direct cost multiplication (2-3x) via duplicate LLM calls on paid Cloud platform. Root cause traced to hardcoded heartbeat + sweep mechanism. Consistent reproduction across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6 and EU/Plus tiers. Primary workflow runs fine but incurs significant hidden cost.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: User demonstrates with trace evidence that duplicate runs appear at ~180s with identical tool call arguments and no preceding model node. 2-3x redundant work confirmed. BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 hardcoded in langgraph-api config/__init__.py. Related issues #6726 and #5672 confirm CancelledError being retried. Clear cost impact on Plus tier Cloud.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared base config metadata dict causing cross-invocation data leakage
signals.summary: ensure_config assigns metadata by reference without copying, so configurable values like thread_id leak into the shared base config metadata dict. After first invocation, all subsequent calls see contaminated metadata from previous invocations, breaking isolation between agents.
signals.review_reason: Causes cross-session state contamination in multi-tenant/multi-agent scenarios. Thread IDs from one invocation bleed into another's metadata. Not a complete block but breaks core isolation guarantees of the checkpointer, causing subtle but serious bugs in production agent systems.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows original_config metadata dict gets mutated after ensure_config call: thread_id from configurable leaks into metadata. Expected {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent'} but got {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'thread_id': 'thread-1'}. 7 comments indicating community interest and confirmation of the bug.

signals.topic: UnboundLocalError crash in push_message when config callbacks is None
signals.summary: push_message in message.py has UnboundLocalError: handlers variable is only assigned inside if/elif branches for BaseCallbackManager or list of BaseCallbackHandler, but is unconditionally referenced on line 360. When config['callbacks'] is None (valid state), neither branch executes and the variable is uninitialized, causing a crash.
signals.review_reason: Direct program crash (UnboundLocalError) when callbacks config is None, which is a valid/expected state in many usage patterns. The code does not handle this gracefully. Causes main workflow failure for affected users.

source_issues.title: Bug: UnboundLocalError in push_message and dead code in _strip_extras
source_issues.evidence: Full code location identified: libs/langgraph/langgraph/graph/message.py lines 351-360. Code shows handlers defined only in if/elif but referenced unconditionally on line 360. No try/catch for the None case. 1 comment confirming the bug.

signals.topic: UnboundLocalError in PregelLoop._first when Command(resume=None) is used
signals.summary: In PregelLoop._first(), the variable resume_is_map is defined only inside the 'if resume is not None' block, but referenced unconditionally on lines 661 and 663. Using Command(resume=None) skips the block and causes UnboundLocalError instead of the expected EmptyInputError.
signals.review_reason: Program crash with UnboundLocalError when using the valid pattern of Command(resume=None) to resume from interrupt. The wrong error type masks the actual issue and prevents proper error handling in user code.

source_issues.title: UnboundLocalError: resume_is_map when using Command(resume=None)
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided: UnboundLocalError at langgraph/pregel/_loop.py line 663 in _first(). Reproducible with minimal code: interrupt node + graph.invoke(Command(resume=None)). Expected EmptyInputError but got UnboundLocalError. 6 comments.

signals.topic: SQLAlchemy DetachedInstanceError causing HTTP 500 on critical endpoints (plugin preferences, forgot password)

signals.review_reason: Two separate critical endpoints (plugin preferences fetch and forgot-password) both fail with DetachedInstanceError returning HTTP 500. Both are key user paths: one blocks the plugin management console, the other blocks account recovery. Root cause is the same SQLAlchemy session lifecycle pattern, warranting merge. count=2 meets the evidence threshold for inclusion.

source_issues.title: sqlalchemy.orm.exc.DetachedInstanceError
source_issues.evidence: GET /console/api/workspaces/current/plugin/preferences/fetch returns HTTP 500 with full SQLAlchemy DetachedInstanceError stack trace. Plugin preferences page in console is completely inaccessible.

source_issues.title: get_account_by_email_with_case_fallback lead account detach instance error

signals.topic: Workflow API returns stuck in 'running' state without final result or log entry
signals.summary: When calling the workflow execution API, requests repeatedly remain in 'running' state indefinitely and do not appear in frontend logs, blocking the primary workflow execution workflow.

Requests hanging in 'running' state with no result and no log entry is a main-process blocking issue that prevents users from obtaining workflow outputs via API.
