source_issues.title: The API endpoint for the workflow request has consistently failed to return the final result.
source_issues.evidence: User reports workflow API requests stay in 'running' state indefinitely and do not appear in frontend logs. API consumer has no way to retrieve results or diagnose the failure.

signals.topic: HTTP Node text size limit configuration not respected — large responses blocked despite env var increase
signals.summary: HTTP Request Node's max text size limit is hard-coded at 1 MB and ignores HTTP_REQUEST_NODE_MAX_TEXT_SIZE environment variable, causing larger API responses to be rejected.
aliases: HTTP request node 1MB cap ignore env var
signals.review_reason: HTTP Node is a core building block in workflows. The size limit config being ignored means users cannot integrate APIs returning responses >1MB even when they explicitly configured higher limits. This is an actionable bug with clear steps to reproduce, not a feature limitation.

source_issues.title: HTTP Node text size limit configuration not taking effect
source_issues.evidence: User increased HTTP_REQUEST_NODE_MAX_TEXT_SIZE and HTTP_REQUEST_NODE_MAX_BINARY_SIZE environment variables but still receives 'Text size is too large, max size is 1.00 MB, but current size is 1.30 MB' error. HTTP Node cannot process legitimate larger API responses.

source_issues.evidence: Dify Cloud shows UI option for 'Microsoft SQL Server' but any query execution results in fatal ModuleNotFoundError. MSSQL integration is completely non-functional on the official Cloud platform.

signals.topic: Vector embedding dimension mismatch causes data corruption and silent failures across agents and vector stores
signals.summary: Embedding dimensions are hardcoded or incorrectly propagated, causing dimension mismatch errors in vector stores (Qdrant, mem0migrations) and blocking writes when agents use different embedding models or Ollama with non-default dimensions.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bug reports (one open, one closed) show a consistent pattern: embedding dimensions are hardcoded or incorrectly propagated, causing vector store write failures. Issue 4801 is actively blocking multi-agent deployments. Issue 4695 (closed) confirms the same root cause pattern with Ollama + Qdrant. Together they form a clear, recurring runtime failure that blocks core memory storage.

source_issues.title: Dimension Mismatch in `mem0migrations` Internal Table
source_issues.evidence: Internal mem0migrations table locks dimensions to first agent's model (e.g., 1024). Second agent with different dimensions (e.g., 512) fails with '[ERROR] expected 1024 dimensions, not 512' on every write.

source_issues.title: Ollama embedding dimensions not propagated to Qdrant vector store (bge-m3: 1024 vs hardcoded 1536)
source_issues.evidence: Ollama bge-m3 model outputs 1024-dim vectors but Qdrant collection is created with hardcoded 1536 dimensions, causing vector write failures.

signals.topic: Client update() API rejects metadata-only and timestamp-only updates with 422 — documented features silently fail on OSS REST server
signals.summary: The Python client advertises and accepts metadata-only and timestamp-only memory updates, but the OSS REST server returns 422 because it requires the 'text' field. Two distinct but related issues causing update failures.

The client advertises features (metadata-only updates, timestamp updates) that the server doesn't support, causing silent failures and 422 errors. Count=2 meets the threshold. Together they break a documented client API path, representing a client-server contract violation that affects all OSS REST users.

source_issues.title: Metadata-only memory updates are accepted by the client but rejected by the OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client accepts update(memory_id, metadata={...}) but OSS server returns 422 because MemoryUpdate.text is required.

source_issues.evidence: Timestamp-only update gets 422. text+timestamp update is accepted but timestamp is silently dropped. Client advertises timestamp as a valid field.

signals.topic: Python client REST API path mismatch — client uses /v1/ prefixes but OSS server uses bare paths, making self-hosted deployments fail on every request

Client always sends /v1/... paths but OSS server uses bare paths. Every CRUD operation fails with 404. Despite being one issue, this is a complete integration path failure for all self-hosted users and meets P1 threshold.

source_issues.title: Custom `host` in the Python client cannot talk to the documented OSS REST server
source_issues.evidence: Client hardcodes /v1/ping/ and /v1/memories/ paths. OSS server only has /memories, /search. Self-hosted user following integration docs gets 404 immediately. All CRUD operations fail.

signals.topic: Ollama embedding endpoint uses wrong path (/v1/embeddings) — mem0 fails with TypeError on all embedding calls when using Ollama
signals.summary: mem0 hardcodes OpenAI-style /v1/embeddings path for all providers. Ollama exposes /api/embeddings, causing 'TypeError: fetch failed' on every search and memory operation when Ollama is the embedding provider.
signals.review_reason: Well-documented bug with clear root cause: mem0 ignores Ollama's actual endpoint and always calls OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings. This causes a hard failure (TypeError: fetch failed) on every memory search and add operation when using Ollama, completely blocking the core memory workflow. The user provided exact reproduction steps and error output. Single issue but evidence is unambiguous and affects a documented integration path.

source_issues.title: mem0 plugin fails with 'TypeError: fetch failed' when using Ollama – wrong embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings)
source_issues.evidence: mem0 always calls POST /v1/embeddings but Ollama only exposes /api/embeddings. Every embedding lookup (search, add) fails with 'TypeError: fetch failed'. EmbeddingsPath override is not applied.

signals.topic: Memory.add() crashes with AttributeError when message content is a list (multimodal format) and vision is disabled — blocks core add flow
signals.summary: parse_vision_messages() unconditionally calls llm.generate_response() without checking if llm is None. When enable_vision=False (default), any message with list-typed content (standard OpenAI/LangChain format) causes AttributeError crash in Memory.add().
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash with full stack trace. The issue is triggered by any message using the standard OpenAI SDK/LangChain list-typed content format — the default multimodal format. This means Memory.add() crashes on the most common real-world input format. The bug is in the default code path, not an edge case. Single issue but the crash is unambiguous and blocks the primary Memory.add() API.

source_issues.title: fix: AttributeError crash in Memory.add() when message content is a list and vision is disabled
source_issues.evidence: Standard OpenAI SDK and LangChain messages use list-typed content [{type:'text', text:'...'}] which is the default multimodal format. When enable_vision=False, parse_vision_messages calls llm.generate_response() on a None llm object, crashing with AttributeError. Full stack trace provided.

signals.topic: BedrockChatClient sends toolConfig.toolChoice without toolConfig.tools when agent has no tools, causing ParamValidationError
signals.summary: When BedrockChatClient is used with an Agent that has no tools, it still sends toolConfig.toolChoice to the AWS Bedrock API without toolConfig.tools, causing a ParamValidationError. This is a regression that breaks the basic chat-only agent workflow.

The bug prevents basic Bedrock chat agents (no tools) from running at all, directly from the official Python client. A prior fix for the same pattern (#4535) already exists, confirming the known regression.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: BedrockChatClient sends `toolConfig.toolChoice` without `toolConfig.tools` when agent has no tools
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproducer shows botocore.exceptions.ParamValidationError: 'Missing required parameter in toolConfig: tools'. Occurs when agent has tools=None. The fix should mirror PR #4535 which addressed a similar tool_choice='none' case. Blocks any Bedrock agent without tools.

signals.topic: BaseChatClient.as_agent() causes TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'function_invocation_configuration'
signals.summary: BaseChatClient.as_agent() accepts a function_invocation_configuration parameter and passes it to Agent.__init__(), but Agent.__init__() does not accept this parameter, causing a TypeError at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Complete TypeError at runtime with a clear root cause trace. Any user who calls as_agent() with function_invocation_configuration encounters this crash immediately. The bug is deterministic and reproducible, blocking the agent creation flow entirely.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: BaseChatClient.as_agent() passes function_invocation_configuration to Agent() which doesn't accept it
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Agent.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'function_invocation_configuration'. Root cause identified in _clients.py lines 86-87: parameter is passed to Agent() which has no **kwargs and no parameter for it. Reproducible by any user who calls as_agent() with function_invocation_configuration.

signals.topic: HandoffBuilder silently drops function-level middleware when cloning agents, breaking logging/observability in handoff workflows

Function middleware (logging, tracing, observability) never executes during handoff workflows without any error or warning. source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: HandoffBuilder drops function-level middleware when cloning agents
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows _clone_chat_agent() passes agent.agent_middleware instead of agent.middleware, dropping @function_middleware. Reproducer provided showing logging/observability middleware never fires during handoff. Affects agent-framework 1.0.0.

signals.topic: playwright-cli kill-all fails to kill daemon processes due to pattern mismatch
signals.summary: The `kill-all` CLI command reports 'No daemon processes found' but daemons survive because the pattern strings ('run-mcp-server', 'run-cli-server', 'cli-daemon') in hyphenated form do not match actual running processes which use camelCase ('cliDaemon.js'). This leads to accumulating orphan processes and ~2.6GB of orphan files in /tmp.
signals.review_reason: User impact is clearly demonstrated: kill-all is completely non-functional, leading to resource accumulation (2.6GB orphan files) and zombie daemon processes. This is a main flow failure — the documented escape hatch for stale daemons does not work.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: playwright-cli kill-all does not kill daemons due to pattern mismatch in killAllDaemons
source_issues.evidence: kill-all reports 'No daemon processes found' but daemons survive. Author accumulated ~55 orphan Firefox Nightly processes and several Chrome orphans in a single day. 2.6GB of orphan files accumulated in /tmp/playwright-artifacts-*. Root cause: patterns 'run-mcp-server', 'run-cli-server', 'cli-daemon' (hyphenated) do not match actual running processes which use 'cliDaemon.js' (camelCase).

signals.topic: Trace viewer snapshot is blank for Stencil.js synthetic-shadow DOM content

signals.review_reason: Critical feature (trace viewer debugging) is unavailable for apps using Stencil.js shadow DOM polyfill. The snapshot panel shows nothing, making debugging impossible for these applications.

source_issues.title: Trace viewer snapshot is blank for content inside Stencil.js synthetic-shadow host elements
source_issues.evidence: Trace viewer snapshot panel is completely blank for any content inside <ion-app> (Stencil.js host element). Root cause identified: snapshotterInjected.js uses node.firstChild/nextSibling which Stencil.js patches at prototype level to return null, hiding children. Affects all Ionic Angular/React/Vue apps using Stencil.

signals.topic: connectOverCDP silently corrupts user downloads by redirecting to temp folder

signals.review_reason: Obvious cost loss and UX degradation: user files silently disappear. Downloads from normal browsing are redirected to temp directories with no notification, causing data loss. Affects AI browser agent use cases where Playwright attaches to user's daily-driver Chrome.

source_issues.title: [Feature] Opt-in to preserve browser-default download behavior when `connectOverCDP` attaches to a user-owned browser
source_issues.evidence: Author lost a 15KB Read.ai transcript and a 1.4GB video download — files disappeared from ~/Downloads and were silently redirected to /tmp/playwright-artifacts-*. 2.6GB of orphan files accumulated. signals.topic: No kernel-level audit trail hooks for agent tool execution, blocking compliance in regulated industries
signals.summary: Semantic Kernel lacks built-in pre/post function execution hooks at the kernel level, preventing users from creating tamper-evident records of agent actions. Two separate users independently raised this need for EU AI Act Article 12 compliance in finance and healthcare deployments.
aliases: no hook point for tamper-evident agent action logging
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report the same gap: no kernel-level hook for pre/post function execution prevents creating tamper-evident audit records. Impact is specific: EU AI Act Article 12 compliance is blocked for finance and healthcare deployments. Users already have production workarounds using MCP servers but note the kernel side requires monkey-patching. This constitutes a workflow-blocking gap for regulated industries, despite being a feature gap rather than a crash.

source_issues.title: Audit trail hooks for agent tool execution
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'For regulated deployments, EU AI Act Article 12 requires automatic event logging that can be independently verified.' Needs pre/post function execution hook at kernel level. User has production implementation for other frameworks and is willing to contribute a PR.

source_issues.title: Audit trail for plugin/function calls
source_issues.evidence: User states: 'For finance and healthcare deployments this is table stakes. An auditor needs to prove that agent X called function Y with argument Z at timestamp T - not just logs that could be altered.' User is running MCP-based workaround in production but notes kernel side doesn't expose a clean hook without monkey-patching.

single query limitation in vector store abstraction

signals.topic: Windows sandbox workspace isolation failure: Everyone SID allows cross-workspace writes
signals.summary: Windows sandbox uses per-workspace capability SIDs but includes the Everyone SID (S-1-1-0) as a restricting SID. Any sandbox session can write to any workspace directory with an Everyone ACE, bypassing per-workspace isolation entirely.
aliases: Windows sandbox isolation broken by Everyone SID
cross-workspace write access in Windows sandbox
signals.review_reason: Security-critical bug: per-workspace sandbox isolation is defeated by the Everyone SID, allowing untrusted sandboxed code to write across workspace boundaries. While based on code analysis rather than empirical testing, the root cause is clearly identifiable in the codebase. This violates the core security guarantee of the sandbox feature and could lead to unauthorized file writes across concurrent sessions.

source_issues.title: Windows sandbox: per-workspace capability SIDs may not isolate workspaces due to Everyone restricting SID
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis shows the restricted token includes the world SID (Everyone, S-1-1-0) as a restricting SID. Any sandbox session — regardless of workspace capability SID — can write to any workspace directory with an Everyone ACE, because the WRITE_RESTRICTED kernel check passes via the world SID, bypassing per-workspace capability SID isolation.

signals.topic: Azure model switch mid-conversation fails with encrypted content decryption error, blocking model changes

This is a complete functional block for users relying on model transitions within a single conversation thread.

signals.topic: Session persistence sanitizer strips required `id` field from built-in tool-call items causing 400 API errors
signals.summary: When using OpenAIConversationsSession for conversation persistence, `_sanitize_openai_conversation_item()` unconditionally strips the `id` field from all conversation items. Built-in tool-call types (file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, web_search_call) require `id` per the OpenAI API spec. The Conversations API returns `400 Missing required parameter: 'items[0].id'` on the second turn onward, blocking multi-turn conversations with these tools.
aliases: id field stripped from tool call items
Missing items[0].id error in session persistence
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn conversation with FileSearchTool/CodeInterpreterTool fails with a hard 400 API error on turn 2+. This is a main-flow blocking bug for users relying on conversation persistence with built-in tool types. The root cause is precisely identified in session_persistence.py: the sanitizer unconditionally pops 'id' from all items, but file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, and web_search_call have required id per the API spec. Workaround exists but does not fix the underlying bug.

signals.topic: Eager sqlite3 import causes deployment failure in environments without sqlite3 (Google Cloud Run Functions)
signals.summary: The agents package eagerly imports sqlite3 at import time. Google Cloud Run Functions uses a base image that does not include sqlite3, causing immediate deployment failure for users who do not use SQLiteSession. No lazy-loading mechanism exists, so the import fires unconditionally regardless of whether sqlite3-dependent features are used.
aliases: sqlite3 import at package load time
Google Cloud Run deployment failure sqlite3 missing
signals.review_reason: Eager sqlite3 import blocks deployment in a common serverless environment (Google Cloud Run Functions). This is a packaging issue causing a hard deployment failure — the app cannot start. The workaround (using a full base image with sqlite3) is non-obvious and requires CI/script changes. The issue demonstrates clear user impact: 'I've had a down server for an hour while I work this out.'

source_issues.title: Don't eagerly import sqlite3
source_issues.evidence: User deployed to Google Cloud Run Function and it failed immediately because agents package imports sqlite3 unconditionally. User explicitly states they are not using any agents features that require sqlite3.

signals.topic: Tracing truncation logic causes RecursionError / stack overflow when LLM response contains None values
signals.summary: In BackendSpanExporter, `_truncate_json_value_for_limit()` calls `_truncated_preview()` for non-str/dict/list values, returning a dict. That dict is then re-entered into `_truncate_mapping_for_json_limit()`, which re-processes the preview dict's keys (including the bool `True` under 'truncated'). This creates an infinite recursion loop under tight budget conditions, resulting in a RecursionError that crashes the trace export and hides the original run error.
aliases: tracing export crashes with None content
signals.review_reason: Tracing export crashes with RecursionError — a hard failure that renders the observability layer unusable and also masks the original error that triggered the truncation. The root cause is a self-referential loop in the truncation logic: _truncated_preview() produces a dict that gets re-entered into the truncation mapper. The trigger condition (LLM response with None) is realistic in production.

source_issues.title: RecursionError in tracing truncation: preview dict recursively re-truncated when message content is None
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible when LLM response contains None in content field and tracing budget is tight. Truncation logic recursively re-processes its own preview dict, causing stack overflow. Traced back to _truncated_preview() returning a dict that is fed back into _truncate_mapping_for_json_limit().

signals.topic: Structured output (`output_type`) suppresses preamble/commentary messages, creating a dead zone during tool execution
signals.summary: When using `output_type` (which maps to text.format: json_schema in the Responses API), the model no longer emits `phase: commentary` messages before tool calls. Users see nothing streamed during tool execution — no 'Let me check...' acknowledgment — creating a noticeable dead zone. This defeats the primary value of preambles (reducing perceived latency). Without `output_type`, preambles work correctly. The issue affects all structured-output agents using tool calls.
aliases: preambles not shown with structured output
no user-visible message before tool calls with output_type
signals.review_reason: Structured output breaks a core UX feature (pre-tool-call preambles). Users get no visible feedback during tool execution when using output_type, which is the standard pattern for structured agent responses. The user identifies this as causing 'perceived latency' degradation. The interaction between json_schema format and the commentary phase appears to be a design issue at the SDK or API level. However, count=1 and the root cause may involve the API rather than the SDK exclusively, so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Preambles with structured output
source_issues.evidence: User demonstrates that with output_type set, the phase: commentary message disappears and the model jumps straight to the function_call. Without output_type, preambles work correctly. The user identifies the impact as a 'noticeable dead zone' during tool execution.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64-encoded file inputs, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: When using prompt caching with base64-encoded file inputs, the cache hit rate drops from 96.7% to 0% on the first file-input round. Subsequent identical file-input requests recover to ~90%. The issue occurs regardless of whether the Agents SDK or the Responses API is used directly. The shared prefix (system instructions, tool definitions) is unchanged between text-only and file-input rounds, yet cache is completely invalidated. This represents significant unexpected cost for mixed text+file workloads.

base64 file input invalidates prompt cache
prompt cache not shared between text and file inputs

This represents a direct cost impact — users lose ~96% cache savings on the first file-input round of every conversation. However, the user acknowledges the issue occurs both in the SDK and the API directly, suggesting the root cause may be at the API level rather than the SDK. Confidence is reduced because the root cause is not confirmed. Count=1 and root cause uncertainty supports P2.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: User shows consistent 0% cache hit on first file-input round across multiple rounds (96.7% for text-only, drops to 0% with file, recovers to 90.3% for repeat file). signals.topic: Pydantic model deserialization failures in multiprocess/forkserver environments with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD
signals.summary: PydanticUserError raised intermittently (~0.6-9.5% rate) when deserializing response models inside multiprocessing forkserver workers, causing main request flow failures and cascading 100% request loss on affected workers.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: ~0.6% intermittent error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true (growing over time, millions of requests processed); ~9.5% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false where ALL requests on affected workers fail due to cached failure. Full stack trace provided showing _get_extra_fields_type → MockCoreSchema → PydanticUserError.

signals.topic: Server-side compaction not emitted on Responses API tool-call-only turns, causing context_length_exceeded
signals.summary: When using Responses API with context_management compaction, no compaction event is emitted during consecutive function_call-only turns. Context grows unbounded until model finally returns a message, risking context_length_exceeded errors in tool-heavy agent loops.
aliases: context_management compaction not triggered for function_call outputs

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with gpt-5.4: input_tokens grow from 5084→5119→5154 across consecutive function_call-only turns with no compaction emitted. Compaction only appears once model returns a message. Agent loops with consecutive tool calls risk hitting context_length_exceeded before compaction is triggered.

signals.topic: Batch API returns 404 model_not_found for GPT-5.x models on /v1/chat/completions endpoint
signals.summary: OpenAI Batch API appends `-batch` suffix to GPT-5.x model names internally, but the suffixed model does not exist, causing 100% of batch requests to fail with model_not_found error on /v1/chat/completions while /v1/responses works fine.
aliases: Batch API GPT-5 model suffix error
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+成本损失：Batch API是成本优化核心功能，GPT-5.x模型在该端点100%失败（request_counts.completed=0, failed=2），完全不可用。Issue提供了GPT-4o对比（工作正常）和/v1/responses对比（也工作正常），证明问题特异于batch+gpt-5组合。Batch作业费用已消耗但全部失败，属直接成本损失。

source_issues.title: OpenAI Batch API returns 404 with GPT-5.x models

Same models work with /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions (non-batch). GPT-4o batch works fine. Clear cost loss: batch jobs fully fail wasting API and compute costs.

signals.topic: Requests blocked with 'Your request was blocked' error when using custom API base URL

source_issues.evidence: All requests blocked when using custom API base URL. Same request succeeds with direct HTTP requests and with litellm library. signals.topic: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt command fails to resume session
signals.summary: When creating persistent sessions, the sessionDir field in the session index JSON is null, causing the `prompt` command to fail with "No acpx session found" even though `status` and `sessions` list the session. This blocks the core user workflow of resuming and continuing conversations in persistent sessions.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it directly blocks the core workflow of resuming persistent sessions. The `prompt` command — the primary way users interact with existing sessions — is completely broken when sessionDir is null. While only 1 issue is filed, this is a critical functional regression: users can create sessions but cannot use them. The issue has clear reproduction steps, identified root cause (sessionDir field not being populated), and affects the main session lifecycle. The session can be created and seen in the index but cannot be resumed, making the persistent session feature effectively unusable for affected users.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions: sessionDir is null, prompt cannot find session
source_issues.evidence: User creates a persistent session with `acpx gemini -s test_session exec`, verifies it exists via `status` and `sessions` commands, but `prompt` fails with 'No acpx session found (searched up to /home/user/workspace)' because sessionDir is null in the index JSON. The session index JSON shows sessionDir: null while cwd and name are set correctly. Root cause identified: status/sessions read the index directly and work, but prompt needs the actual session directory which cannot be resolved from null.

signals.topic: WSL to Windows cwd path translation: Windows .exe agents fail to spawn due to Linux-style paths
signals.summary: When ACPX embedded runtime runs on WSL and spawns Windows .exe agents (e.g., copilot.exe), the cwd passed to session/new is a Linux POSIX path that Windows agents cannot resolve, causing session creation to fail with a 'Directory does not exist' error.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it blocks the agent spawning workflow for WSL users who want to use Windows-native agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot CLI). The session/new request fails with a descriptive error, making it impossible to use Windows executables as agents from within WSL. The root cause is clearly identified (asAbsoluteCwd() produces POSIX paths on WSL) and the issue provides a concrete proposed fix. While count=1 and single-repo, the user impact is significant: a core platform combination (WSL + Windows agents) is entirely broken, with clear error messages and reproduction steps. Cross-referenced with openclaw/openclaw#42557 indicating this is a known class of bugs.

source_issues.title: WSL→Windows cwd path translation when spawning Windows .exe agents from WSL
source_issues.evidence: User on WSL2 configures a Windows .exe agent (copilot.exe) and attempts to spawn an ACP session. The gateway passes a Linux path `/home/user/.openclaw/workspace` to session/new, and the Windows agent returns error code -32603 with 'Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed: /home/user/.openclaw/workspace'. Root cause identified: asAbsoluteCwd() uses path.resolve() which always produces POSIX paths on Linux/WSL, and these are sent directly to Windows agents. Multiple path format tests show Linux paths fail while Windows native, UNC, and wslpath-converted paths succeed.

signals.topic: VirusTotal Code Insight false positives block legitimate skill publication
signals.summary: Multiple skill publishers report that VirusTotal Code Insight incorrectly flags their benign skills as 'Suspicious', even when OpenClaw's own scanner returns Benign/High Confidence. This prevents legitimate skills from being published with a clean security banner, causing direct user impact on skill discoverability and trust.
aliases: VT Code Insight incorrectly flags benign skills as suspicious
skill security banner shows Suspicious despite benign scan
signals.review_reason: This is a high-frequency (8 distinct skills), multi-day ongoing issue where legitimate skill publishers cannot get a clean security banner despite OpenClaw's own scanner returning Benign/High Confidence. The VirusTotal Code Insight system is applying generic security heuristics (e.g., 'transaction', 'wallet', 'USDC', 'subprocess', 'crypto') that generate false positives for financial tools, CLI integrations, and any skill using standard developer patterns (curl|bash, cookie auth, Bearer tokens). The direct user impact is: (1) skill trust/sales is undermined by a Suspicious banner shown to all visitors, (2) legitimate payment and crypto-adjacent skills are systematically disadvantaged, (3) OpenClaw's own benign verdict is being overridden by VirusTotal. Multiple authors explicitly note their skills pass OpenClaw's own scanner — indicating the platform's own detection is working correctly but being undermined by VirusTotal integration.

signals.topic: Registry metadata scanner bug flags legitimate credential-declaring skills as Suspicious
signals.summary: The OpenClaw security scanner compares SKILL.md content against a registry summary that lacks fields for env vars, credentials, and homepage. The scanner reports 'Required env vars: none' even when skills properly declare OLOSTEP_API_KEY, and the author identified at least 4 other affected skills (venice-api-kit, firecrawl-search, aikek, getpost-scrape). This is a systemic bug causing widespread false Suspicious verdicts.

However, it is represented by a single issue (count=1) and lacks external corroboration beyond the author's own testing. Priority is P2 because while the bug is real and impactful (affects at least 5 skills), it requires platform-level schema fix and is not a blocking user-facing flow failure. signals.topic: Default subprocess timeout of 20 seconds too short, causing intermittent workflow failures

Users get intermittent 'lobster subprocess timed out' errors with no visibility.
signals.review_reason: While only one user reported this, the impact is concrete — intermittent failures affecting multiple cron jobs in production, with a clear root cause (hardcoded 20s default). The symptom (intermittent subprocess timeout) causes unpredictable workflow failures that are hard to debug, representing a cost-loss and experience degradation.

source_issues.title: feat: configurable default timeoutMs for workflow execution

signals.topic: Bedrock Converse async streaming: @retry_decorator silently inert on async generator functions
signals.summary: The `_conversion_stream_with_retry` async function in bedrock_converse utils.py uses `yield`, making it an async generator. Tenacity's `@retry_decorator` cannot intercept exceptions during async generator iteration — it only wraps the initial call, which merely creates the generator object. As a result, retries never fire for streaming calls that encounter retryable errors (ThrottlingException, ServiceUnavailableException). This is a silent failure that silently drops streaming chunks on transient AWS errors.
aliases: tenacity retry on async generator not working
signals.review_reason: Streaming is a core feature path. When transient AWS errors occur during streaming, the retry mechanism is completely inert — the exception propagates silently without any retry attempt. This means users' streaming workflows fail unpredictably on recoverable errors. The silent nature (no traceback) makes diagnosis difficult. Single-reporter but root cause is clearly confirmed with a reproduction script.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: @retry_decorator on async generator _conversion_stream_with_retry is silently inert
source_issues.evidence: Streaming calls to Bedrock Converse with transient errors (ThrottlingException, ServiceUnavailableException) silently fail with no retries. The tenacity decorator never fires because the function is an async generator. The bug is silent — no traceback, retries simply never trigger.

When a user introduces context in turn 1 ('my name is Laurie') and asks about it in turn 2, the agent returns empty — this completely breaks conversational memory. The official documentation shows this pattern should work. Single-reporter but the bug is trivially reproducible and directly contradicts documented behavior.

signals.topic: CLI command parser greedy first-match causes silent mis-routing of lazy-loaded subcommands (daemon, doctor, etc.)
signals.summary: CommandParser.parse() uses greedy first-match walk: when argv contains a lazy-loaded command name (daemon, doctor, embeddings) followed by a core sync command name (start, status, task), the parser resolves to the core command instead. ruflo daemon start silently runs the top-level start command, leaving the daemon not running. No error is raised.
signals.review_reason: Silent command mis-routing causes wrong behavior without any error or warning. The user runs 'ruflo daemon start' expecting a daemon to run, but the top-level start command executes instead and the daemon is not started. The daemon status check via 'ruflo doctor' reports 'Not running' with only a warning (not an error). This is a UX trust violation: the system appears to work but does not do what the user asked. The root cause is well-documented at CommandParser.parse() lines 136-143 in packages/@claude-flow/cli/src/parser.ts. Affects all lazy-loaded commands when combined with core sync command names in argv — a broad surface area.

source_issues.title: CLI: lazy-loaded commands silently mis-route when a core sync command name follows in argv
source_issues.evidence: ruflo -v daemon start --foreground executes top-level start instead of daemon start subcommand. Confirmed via debug output showing 'Executing: start' with positional ['daemon']. No error raised. Affects all lazy-loaded commands (daemon, doctor, embeddings, neural, config, workflow, hive-mind) combined with any core sync command name (init, start, status, task, session, agent, swarm, memory, mcp, hooks). Daemon appears not running per ruflo doctor, but no warning given.

signals.topic: Chrome browser fails to start in containerized/Linux environments due to sandbox restrictions, with no way to pass --no-sandbox via Agent Dashboard UI
signals.summary: Chrome exits immediately on Linux containers, VMs, CI runners, and Ubuntu 23.10+ environments with 'No usable sandbox!' error. The Agent Dashboard UI has no option to configure launch arguments, making browser sessions unusable in these environments. Issue #1213 documents this for the UI path; issue #70 documents it for CLI. Root cause is a missing launch args configuration mechanism in the Agent Dashboard and insufficient CLI flags for container use.
aliases: browser session fails on Linux Server/NAS
signals.review_reason: Chrome cannot start in containerized environments due to sandbox restrictions, which is a well-documented Chromium limitation (crbug.com/638180). Issue #1213 shows the Agent Dashboard lacks any mechanism to pass --no-sandbox, directly blocking users in Linux containers, VMs, CI runners, and hardened environments. Issue #70 shows the same problem for CLI in cloud container environments. Issue #1035 shows the tool hangs completely on Linux Server/NAS environments. These are not edge cases — containers and cloud VMs are standard deployment targets for AI coding agents. The product is non-functional in these environments.

source_issues.title: Add Chrome launch args support in Agent Dashboard UI (needed for `--no-sandbox` on some Linux/VM/container setups)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome exits early with 'FATAL:content/browser/zygote_host/zygote_host_impl_linux.cc:128] No usable sandbox!' on Linux containers/VMs/CI. Agent Dashboard UI has no option to pass --no-sandbox, --disable-dev-shm-usage, or --disable-gpu. Session fails immediately without exposing DevTools URL.

source_issues.title: Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported. See https://crbug.com/638180.
source_issues.evidence: Chrome crashes with 'Page crashed' when running as root in containerized cloud environments (Claude Code on Web). No CLI flag or env var for --no-sandbox. AI coding agents in cloud containers are completely blocked.

source_issues.title: agent-browser open hangs on Linux Server/NAS - daemon fails to start (OpenClaw agent)
source_issues.evidence: On Linux Server/NAS (Ubuntu 24.04), agent-browser open hangs indefinitely. No socket file is ever created, Chrome process never starts. Possibly related to sandbox/display requirements. Blocks headless server/CI use cases.

signals.topic: --cdp attach to existing Chrome instance hangs indefinitely on macOS, blocking integration with externally-managed Chrome sessions
signals.summary: When using --cdp to attach to an externally-launched Chrome instance on macOS, the daemon hangs forever with no output or timeout. Users cannot reuse existing Chrome sessions (e.g., with pre-existing auth state) and must fall back to raw CDP HTTP calls or let agent-browser launch its own Chrome. Also causes duplicate remote-debugging permission prompts due to incorrect websocket path priority.
signals.review_reason: Issue #1193 is a confirmed reproducible hang: agent-browser --cdp attach to an existing Chrome instance on macOS hangs indefinitely with no timeout, no error, and no recovery. The user must kill the daemon manually. This blocks the core integration use case of attaching to an externally-managed Chrome session with pre-existing auth state. Issue #1206/#1210 adds that even when it doesn't hang, --auto-connect triggers duplicate permission prompts because the websocket path from DevToolsActivePort is not tried first. Together these represent a significant workflow degradation for the primary attach-to-existing-Chrome use case.

source_issues.title: --cdp attach to existing Chrome instance hangs indefinitely on macOS (Chrome 139)
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser tab list --cdp 9222 hangs forever on macOS when attaching to externally-launched Chrome. Daemon starts and creates socket but never returns. Users must fall back to raw CDP HTTP. Confirmed with multiple Chrome versions (139, 144+). Root cause: daemon gets stuck in target discovery for externally-launched Chrome with HTTP discovery path.

source_issues.title: Is it normal to always have to allow twice when connecting to an existing Chrome instance via --auto-connect?
source_issues.evidence: --auto-connect causes two separate remote-debugging permission prompts: one during legacy discovery probing and another for the real websocket attach. Issue #1210 identifies root cause as incorrect websocket path priority — DevToolsActivePort path should be tried first.

source_issues.title: Prefer DevToolsActivePort websocket path first in --auto-connect to avoid duplicate remote-debugging prompts
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: --auto-connect reads DevToolsActivePort then calls legacy discovery (/json/version, /json/list) before falling back to the exact websocket path. Should try the DevToolsActivePort ws:// path first. Causes duplicate browser-side permission prompts.

signals.topic: Closing a tab that appears before the active tab silently retargets the session to the wrong page
signals.summary: In multi-tab workflows, running 'tab close N' on a tab with an index lower than the current active tab causes active_page_index to not decrement, silently moving the session to a different page. Subsequent commands run against the wrong target. Root cause is in browser.rs where active_index is only clamped on out-of-range but not adjusted for pre-active removals.
aliases: tab close silently changes active page
active page index corruption on tab close
signals.review_reason: This is a correctness bug in multi-tab workflows where the session silently changes scope after a tab close operation. The user does not switch tabs, but subsequent commands run against a different page without any indication. This is a critical correctness issue for any agent workflow that manages multiple tabs, as commands can silently operate on the wrong page (e.g., reading sensitive data from the wrong tab, submitting forms to the wrong context). The root cause is clearly identified and reproducible.

source_issues.title: `tab close` of an earlier tab can silently retarget the active page
source_issues.evidence: With tabs [A,B,C,D] and C active, closing tab 0 causes active_page_index to stay at 2, pointing at D instead of C. Commands after tab close silently target the wrong page. Root cause identified in cli/src/native/browser.rs: active-index update only handles out-of-range case, not pre-active removals.

signals.topic: Using --profile causes session to lose the active page after the first command, falling back to about:blank on macOS
signals.summary: On macOS, agent-browser works correctly without --profile, but with a persistent profile directory the second command in a session loses the active page and reports about:blank. The first open succeeds but subsequent commands (tab list, get url) show the wrong target. Daemon log shows WebSocket connection reset. This breaks any workflow relying on profile persistence (e.g., reusing browser auth state across commands).
aliases: --profile session loses page after first command
about:blank instead of actual page after profile open
signals.review_reason: Profile persistence is essential for reusing browser auth state (logged-in sessions, cookies, etc.) across agent commands. When --profile is used, the session loses the active page after the first command, making profile-based workflows completely unreliable. The user must either abandon profile persistence entirely or work around it by launching Chrome without profile, losing all browser state. This is a blocking issue for any real-world workflow that needs persistent browser state across commands.

source_issues.title: `--profile` sessions lose the active page after the first command and fall back to `about:blank`
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: open succeeds and shows correct URL, but next command 'tab list' shows about:blank. Daemon log shows 'WebSocket Error: WebSocket protocol error: Connection reset without closing handshake'. Works correctly without --profile. Affects macOS 15.3 with Chrome profile version 147.0.7727.56.

signals.topic: Browser extension approval popups (e.g., MetaMask signature/connect flows) are not surfaced as controllable pages, causing command timeouts
signals.summary: When a site action triggers an extension approval popup (e.g., MetaMask connect or transaction signature on https://metamask.github.io/test-dapp/), agent-browser does not surface the spawned popup as a controllable target. Commands hang until timeout. This blocks any workflow requiring extension interaction, including Web3 wallet operations, password managers, and other extension-gated approvals.
signals.review_reason: Extension approval popups (MetaMask connect, signature, and transaction flows) are fundamental to Web3/browser-extension-based workflows. When agent-browser cannot surface these popups as controllable targets, any workflow requiring extension interaction (wallet connections, transaction approvals, password manager unlocks) is blocked. The command hangs without any indication that a popup appeared, making it impossible to automate extension-dependent flows.

source_issues.title: Spawned browser extension popups are not controllable from agent-browser
source_issues.evidence: When MetaMask triggers an approval popup on https://metamask.github.io/test-dapp/, the popup target is not surfaced as a controllable page. Commands hang until timeout. Extension content scripts are injected correctly but popup windows are not tracked as targets.

signals.topic: Vertex AI: streamFunctionCallArguments breaks all tool calls — both array arguments never emit (14358) and unconditional config breaks unary API (14314)
signals.summary: Two distinct but same-root bugs: (1) Array-typed tool arguments never trigger tool-call events on Vertex because the terminal streaming chunk omits 'willContinue', and (2) a v4.0.106 regression unconditionally adds streaming function call config to all Vertex unary API calls, causing 100% of generateText/generateObject calls to fail with 400.
signals.review_reason: Two high-impact bugs: one causes all tool executions with array args to silently never run, the other is a critical regression (v4.0.106 released 2026-04-09) causing 100% of Vertex unary API calls to fail. Both are active regressions with reproduction steps. Combined count=2.

source_issues.title: streamFunctionCallArguments: tool-call never emitted for array args (terminal chunk has partialArgs)
source_issues.evidence: tool-input-start and tool-input-delta events fire correctly but tool-input-end and tool-call are never emitted. Tool's execute function is never called. Simple non-array args work.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex@4.0.106: unconditional streamFunctionCallArguments breaks all Vertex unary API calls
source_issues.evidence: ALL generateText/generateObject calls on Vertex return 400 after upgrading to 4.0.106: 'Unable to submit request because streaming function call is not supported in unary API.' 100% regression across all Vertex models. Streaming endpoint not affected.

signals.topic: Google provider: Gemini tool calls with $ref/$defs in function responses fail with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT
signals.summary: When a tool returns a raw JS object containing JSON Schema $ref/$defs (common with Zod v4's z.lazy()), the Google provider sends it directly to Gemini's functionResponse.content. Gemini interprets $ref pointers and rejects with 400, breaking all tool-use workflows with recursive schemas.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: tool execution path breaks with 400 error, blocking all multi-step tool-use workflows using recursive Zod schemas. Clear API-level rejection with full reproduction provided. This is a regression for any user with z.lazy() schemas.

source_issues.title: Gemini rejects `$ref`/`$defs` in function response content (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT)
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: 'The referenced name `#/$defs/__schema0` in function_response.response does not match to a display_name in the function_response.parts.' Full reproduction code provided. Affects all users using Zod v4 recursive schemas with Google provider tool calls.

signals.topic: Anthropic structured outputs fail with valid Zod schemas due to unsupported JSON Schema keywords
signals.summary: Anthropic's API strictly validates output_config.format.schema, rejecting valid Zod schemas that contain unsupported keywords like exclusiveMinimum, not, minimum, maximum. This causes 400 errors on structured output calls that would work correctly with Anthropic's own SDK.
aliases: Anthropic structured output 400 Zod schema keywords
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: structured output calls (a key feature) fail with 400 on valid Zod schemas. The same schemas work with Anthropic's own SDK, confirming the issue is in the Vercel AI SDK's schema conversion. Full reproduction provided.

source_issues.title: Anthropic structured outputs fail with valid Zod schemas due to unsupported JSON Schema keywords (e.g. exclusiveMinimum, not, minimum, maximum)
source_issues.evidence: Valid Zod schemas cause 400 errors from Anthropic API because unsupported JSON Schema keywords are passed through without sanitization. Anthropic's own SDK handles this via zodOutputFormat/jsonSchemaOutputFormat helpers. Full reproduction provided.

signals.topic: convertToModelMessages omits 'input' on tool-call parts when input is undefined, causing OpenAI 'Missing required parameter' error on chat history replay
signals.summary: When a tool UI part has state 'output-available' but no input field (tool with no parameters), convertToModelMessages produces a tool-call ModelMessage without 'input'. The OpenAI provider sends this to the API without 'arguments', triggering OpenAI's 'Missing required parameter: input[N].arguments' error. This permanently breaks chat history replay.
aliases: OpenAI missing required parameter arguments tool-call replay
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure with permanent consequence: chat history replay is permanently broken for tools with no parameters. This is a data corruption issue — once messages are persisted, the conversation cannot recover. Clear API-level error with reproduction provided.

source_issues.title: BUG: `convertToModelMessages` omits `input` on tool-call parts when `input` is undefined, causing OpenAI 'Missing required parameter: arguments' error
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI returns 'Missing required parameter: input[N].arguments' when replaying chat history containing tool-call messages from tools with no parameters. Once persisted and replayed, the conversation is permanently stuck. Full reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes stream before async transform registers tool, causing tool results to be silently lost
signals.summary: In runToolsTransformation, the outstandingToolResults counter is incremented after an await parseToolCall(), but flush can fire during that await and see counter=0, closing the stream prematurely. Tool results are silently lost — never returned to the caller.
aliases: runToolsTransformation race condition lost tool results
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss bug in core stream processing: tool results are permanently dropped with no error signal to the user. Consistently reproducible in Bun runtime. Even though count=1, the silent data loss nature and core-level impact warrants P0.

source_issues.title: Race condition in runToolsTransformation: flush closes stream before async transform registers tool
source_issues.evidence: Race condition consistently reproduced in Bun v1.3.11 when synchronous I/O (SQLite reads) in tool registration pauses the event loop during the await parseToolCall() window. Tool results are silently lost with no error thrown. Demonstrates data loss scenario.

signals.topic: next/font/google build failure in Turbopack — font resolution broken in 16.2.x
signals.summary: When using Turbopack (the default bundler in Next.js 16), next/font/google fails during production build with multiple errors: 'http2 feature is not enabled' (Rust panic in hyper-util), CSS module resolution failure, and Google Fonts fetch failure. This regression started in 16.2.2 and persists in 16.2.3. Users cannot patch the CVE-2026-23869 security fix (CVSS 7.5) without breaking their build, creating a forced trade-off between security and functionality.
signals.review_reason: Build is completely blocked for users of the default bundler (Turbopack) in Next.js 16.2.x. The regression forces users to choose between staying on a vulnerable version (CVE-2026-23869, CVSS 7.5) or upgrading and losing font functionality. This is a critical P0: build-time blocking, affects all users using next/font/google with Turbopack, and has clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: next/font/google fails to build on 16.2.3 — Turbopack font resolution broken
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with Rust panic 'http2 feature is not enabled' in hyper-util, CSS module resolution failure, and Google Fonts fetch failure. Regression from 16.1.7 to 16.2.2/16.2.3. Users forced to choose between patching CVE-2026-23869 and having a working build.

signals.topic: BFCache hydration failure in dev mode — browser back/forward navigation renders dead page
signals.summary: In Next.js 16 dev mode, using the browser back button after a hard navigation (typing URL in address bar) causes React to enter a 'dead' state on the restored BFCache page. No component lifecycle runs, no hooks execute, no console logs fire, and any state becomes permanently suspended. No errors are thrown, making it silently broken. Works correctly in production deployments.
aliases: browser back button dead after hard navigation dev mode
signals.review_reason: Navigation flow is completely broken in local dev mode. Back button is a core navigation mechanism and silently fails without any error output, making it extremely hard to debug. Users lose state and get stuck on loading screens. Although count=1, the severity is high: silent complete failure of a primary browser navigation path, with real user impact reported (auth sessions stuck).

source_issues.title: [Next 16 / React 19] Hydration Failure on BFCache restore after using browser back and forward button in dev mode
source_issues.evidence: Browser displays cached HTML but JavaScript is completely dead. No component lifecycle runs, no console.log fires, state/hooks become permanently suspended with zero console errors. Back navigation works in production but not in local dev. Causes session pending issues in real apps using better-auth.

signals.topic: Dev server aborts (Rust panic) when error overlay renders multi-byte UTF-8 characters — terminal-width sensitive crash
signals.summary: The next-code-frame Rust crate panics with 'end byte index X is not a char boundary' when rendering the dev error overlay with multi-byte UTF-8 characters (e.g. Japanese). The crash is terminal-width sensitive, meaning the same app may or may not crash depending on how many display columns the overlay uses. The dev server aborts entirely, blocking all debugging.
aliases: Dev server aborts: next-code-frame panic on multi-byte source (terminal width)
Rust panic in next-code-frame with UTF-8
signals.review_reason: Dev server crashes and aborts entirely when a runtime error contains multi-byte UTF-8 characters, which is common in internationalized apps. This completely blocks the error debugging experience. The crash is non-deterministic (terminal-width dependent), making it hard to reproduce and diagnose. P1 despite count=1 due to complete dev server abort with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: [Error Overlay] Dev server aborts: next-code-frame panic on multi-byte source (terminal width)
source_issues.evidence: Rust panic at 'crates/next-code-frame/src/highlight.rs:1011:45' with 'fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting'. Dev server aborts when rendering error overlay with multi-byte characters. Crash is terminal-width sensitive, reproducible by resizing terminal. Blocks debugging entirely on the affected page.

signals.topic: Turbopack next build passes 'development' environment to SWC plugins instead of 'production'
signals.summary: When running 'next build' with Turbopack (the default in Next.js 16), SWC transform plugins receive 'development' as the environment via TransformPluginMetadataContextKind::Env instead of 'production'. This causes SWC plugins to behave incorrectly during production builds, e.g., bundling all translation keys instead of splitting per-environment, resulting in +1.4MB of extra JavaScript in production bundles.
aliases: Turbopack passes 'development' to SWC plugins during next build
signals.review_reason: Production builds get incorrect environment context, causing measurable bundle bloat (+1.4MB in a real production site). This is not a cosmetic issue — SWC plugins make production-specific optimizations that fail to trigger, directly impacting end-user performance. Root cause is a hardcoded 'development' string in Turbopack source. Clear user impact evidence with specific byte count.

source_issues.title: Turbopack passes 'development' to SWC plugins during next build
source_issues.evidence: Production build with Turbopack incorrectly passes 'development' env to SWC plugins (hardcoded in turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-plugins/src/transform/swc_ecma_transform_plugins.rs). Real site (galaxus.ch) reports +1.4MB extra JS transferred due to translation plugin bundling all keys instead of splitting per-env.

signals.topic: Turbopack dev server enters panic loop on Windows with pnpm — 'Next.js package not found' and ChunkLoadError
signals.summary: On Windows with pnpm, running 'next dev' (Turbopack) causes a FATAL panic loop with 'Next.js package not found' errors. The terminal repeatedly prints 'FATAL: An unexpected Turbopack error occurred' and the browser receives ChunkLoadError for HMR chunks. The dev server becomes unusable, forcing users to fall back to --webpack mode or clear the .next cache (temporarily).
aliases: Turbopack panic loop on Windows with pnpm
signals.review_reason: Complete dev server failure (panic loop) that makes development impossible on a common platform combination (Windows + pnpm + Turbopack). This is P0: the dev server crashes repeatedly, HMR fails, and users are forced to fall back to webpack. Windows is a primary platform and pnpm is a widely-used package manager, making this a high-impact blocking issue for a significant user segment.

source_issues.title: Turbopack panic loop on Windows with pnpm: Next.js package not found + ChunkLoadError on /dashboard
source_issues.evidence: FATAL panic loop: 'Failed to write app endpoint /dashboard/page', 'Caused by: Next.js package not found'. Browser shows ChunkLoadError for HMR chunk. Dev server is completely unusable. node_modules is correctly resolved via pnpm symlink. Workaround is --webpack mode. Windows + pnpm + Turbopack combination is a common real-world setup.

signals.topic: vercel.projects.createProject silently removed support for secret environment variable type, breaking existing user code without warnings
signals.summary: The projects.createProject SDK method no longer accepts 'secret' type for environment variables, breaking production code without deprecation notice or documentation update.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow breaking change — projects.createProject silently dropped support for 'secret' environment variable type, causing user production code to break. The silent nature (no deprecation notice, no docs warning) makes it a clear user pain point affecting real workflows. Count=1 prevents P0, but the severity of a silent breaking change affecting project creation in production warrants P1.

source_issues.title: [BREAKING CHANGE|DOC ISSUE]: vercel.projects.createProject no longer support secret vars so it breaks current code
source_issues.evidence: User reports a silent breaking change that removed the 'secret' type from environment variable creation in projects.createProject, causing their production code to break. No deprecation warning or documentation notice was provided. The docs also fail to explain the differences between system, secret, encrypted, plain, and sensitive types.

signals.topic: Git source control filter (`[ref..ref]`) fails to detect changes compared to native git
signals.summary: When using `--filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"`, turbo does not detect changes that `git show origin/main..HEAD` correctly identifies. The `--affected` flag works but the git-ref-based filter syntax is broken, breaking CI/CD change-detection workflows.
aliases: source control filter not detecting changes
signals.review_reason: This is a real user workflow failure: turbo's git-ref-based change-detection filter silently misses changes that git correctly identifies. Users relying on `[origin/main..HEAD]` style filters in CI have no working turbo-based change detection. While count=1, the impact is significant as it breaks core CI/CD change-detection pipelines, and the workaround (`--affected`) is not equivalent for all use cases.

source_issues.title: Filtering by source control changes doesn't detect changes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows `git show origin/main..HEAD` outputs changes but `turbo run lint --dry=json --filter="[origin/main..HEAD]"` outputs no directories. Only `--affected` flag works as workaround.

signals.topic: Turbo > 2.8.14 regression: fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache with custom CA certificates
signals.summary: Introduced in turbo > 2.8.14 (likely related to ApiClient fast-client refactoring), turbo intermittently fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache servers (e.g., ducktors/turborepo-remote-cache) when custom CA certificates are used. Remote cache is unavailable and build results are not cached, causing repeated full builds and wasted CI time.
aliases: custom CA remote cache connection failure
remote cache not working with custom certificates
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact regression: turbo silently fails to use remote cache when custom CA certificates are in use, resulting in 100% cache miss and full rebuilds on every run. The issue is confirmed as a regression from 2.8.14, is reproducible with a dedicated test repo, and affects self-hosted cache deployments widely used in enterprise environments. The connection failure is intermittent but high-probability, making it a consistent workflow blocker.

source_issues.title: Turbo > 2.8.14 fails to connect to self-hosted remote cache server with custom CA
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction repo provided. Error: 'Remote caching unavailable (Could not connect to "https://my-hostname:3000/")'. Works with turbo <= 2.8.14, broken in > 2.8.14. Likelihood increases with more certificates in CA file. Affects both macOS ARM64 and Linux AMD64.

signals.topic: Terminal ANSI color codes lost and code line links broken when turbo streams task output
signals.summary: When turbo runs tasks with `--ui="stream"` (default behavior), ANSI color codes in task output are stripped and IDE-clickable file:line links are broken. Users lose the ability to click error/warning lines in their terminal (e.g., WebStorm, iTerm) to jump to source, and colors distinguishing warnings from errors disappear.
aliases: colors not preserved in turbo output
IDE clickable links not working with turbo
terminal color codes stripped by turbo stream
signals.review_reason: This is a UX degradation: developers lose color-coded severity distinction (warnings vs errors) and IDE click-to-navigate functionality when using turbo's streaming UI. While it doesn't block builds, it measurably degrades the developer experience in a daily-use tool, slowing down error investigation. Issue is reproducible and documented with screenshots.

source_issues.title: Colors are not preserved, code lines are not clickable
source_issues.evidence: User provides side-by-side screenshots showing warnings yellow and errors red when running directly, vs all monochrome when running through turbo. Clicking line numbers in iTerm/WebStorm works directly but not through turbo. Affected on Mac with iTerm and WebStorm.

signals.topic: Timed-out tasks do not flush logs, making CI failure debugging impossible
signals.summary: When a turbo task times out in CI, turbo does not flush or output any logs for that task, leaving no way to determine which task timed out or what progress it made before timing out. Users see only 'The action has timed out' without any task context.
signals.review_reason: This directly blocks CI debugging: when a task times out, developers get no logs from the failed task, making it impossible to determine which task failed or what it was doing. This is a recurring CI issue that causes significant time loss investigating silent failures. The fact that logs may never have started (turbo may not have begun processing the task) makes this particularly severe for CI reliability.

source_issues.title: Tasks that time out are not flushing logs
source_issues.evidence: CI log shows task timeout with no preceding task output: task started but logs never appeared, then 'The action has timed out' with no task context. Author confirms this happens infrequently but enough to cause havoc in CI.

signals.topic: Rust runtime v2 fails with "address already in use" error in `vercel dev` causing function invocations to fail
signals.summary: Rust beta runtime crashes on function invocation in `vercel dev` with EADDRINUSE error, preventing the Rust runtime from functioning locally.
signals.review_reason: Rust runtime v2 crash on EADDRINUSE is a runtime failure that prevents the Rust beta runtime from functioning in `vercel dev`. This is a clear functional breakage of a beta feature, confirmed by the OS-level error and related prior issue #14532 indicating it is not an isolated incident. Although count=1, the repeated nature and the fact it renders a runtime completely non-functional justifies P1.

source_issues.title: Rust runtime v2 fails with "address already in use"
source_issues.evidence: Rust beta runtime crashes with EADDRINUSE error on every function invocation in `vercel dev`, making the runtime unusable locally. References related issue #14532, indicating a known/repeated problem.

signals.topic: Vercel CLI `vercel env add` ignores `--yes --force` flags and prompts for git branch in CI/CD environments
signals.summary: The `vercel env add <name> preview` command always prompts interactively for a git branch even when all non-interactive flags are provided, making it impossible to automate environment variable creation in CI/CD pipelines.
aliases: vercel env add interactive prompt cannot be bypassed in CI
signals.review_reason: The `--yes --force --non-interactive` flags are completely ignored by `vercel env add preview`, causing the CLI to hang interactively in CI/CD environments. This is a clear workflow-blocking bug that forces users to bypass the CLI entirely and use the REST API directly. The evidence shows the CLI's own hint suggests a fix that doesn't work, confirming a bug rather than a configuration issue.

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env add <name> preview` always prompts for git branch even with --yes --force
source_issues.evidence: CLI command hangs in CI/CD environments (e.g. GitHub Actions) because the interactive prompt cannot be bypassed. The CLI's own error output suggests a fix command, but that exact command still triggers the same prompt, indicating a bug in flag handling. User must fall back to Vercel REST API as workaround.

signals.topic: Vercel CLI cannot specify project for commands in monorepo setups, causing forced interaction and broken scripts/agents
signals.summary: In monorepos with multiple projects, the CLI lacks a working option to specify the target project for commands. The `--project` flag does not work for most commands, forcing unintended project selection and breaking automation scripts and coding agents.
aliases: monorepo project selection not supported in CLI
CLI cannot target specific project in monorepo
signals.review_reason: Monorepo project targeting limitation is a real UX and automation pain, but with count=1 and no explicit blocking evidence (no CI failure or crash described), it falls into the feature gap/enhancement category. Kept because it demonstrably breaks scripts and agents, but downgraded to P2 given single-occurrence and lack of full workflow blockage evidence.

source_issues.title: CLI Monorepo Forced Interaction
source_issues.evidence: User reports that the CLI does not provide a way to specify which project to run commands on in a monorepo. The `--project` flag is described as not working for most commands. This interferes with automation scripts and coding agents that expect deterministic project targeting.

signals.topic: Database migration failure causing fallback to in-memory storage on every project open
signals.summary: Migration mismatch at step 36 causes Zed to fall back to in-memory database, losing project state on every editor open
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking - database migration mismatch causes complete fallback to in-memory storage on every project open. Causes persistent data loss for all project state (settings, workspace metadata). Repeated occurrence on every launch makes this a high-impact issue.

source_issues.title: Failed to load the database file.
source_issues.evidence: Migration changed for WorkspaceDb at step 36 - ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD COLUMN active_mode vs ALTER TABLE remote_connections ADD COLUMN remote_env. Falls back to in-memory database (WARN [db] Opening fallback in-memory database). All project state, settings, and workspace data are lost on every startup. Warning notification appears on every project open.

signals.topic: Unsupported GPU modal completely blocks editor on clean/new profile
signals.summary: GPU detection modal prevents any editor interaction until user manually dismisses it
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking - modal completely prevents editor use until manual user interaction. Severely impacts CI/automation workflows and bug triage where new/dirty profiles are frequently created.

source_issues.title: Unsupported GPU modal blocks the editor on a clean profile (llvmpipe)
source_issues.evidence: On software stack without discrete GPU (llvmpipe), a centered Unsupported GPU dialog appears. signals.topic: Local Ollama models unavailable when offline despite being locally running
signals.summary: Local Ollama models disappear from model selection when internet disconnected
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation - local models should work offline but require internet connectivity for model discovery. Core value proposition of local models (privacy, offline availability) is broken.

source_issues.title: Can't use local ollama models while offline
source_issues.evidence: When offline, local Ollama models do not appear in the model selection list even when Ollama is running locally. Models only appear when connected to the internet. Users who rely on local models for privacy/cost reasons cannot use them offline.

signals.topic: External ACP agent history completely broken - new chats overwrite previous sessions
signals.summary: ACP external agent sessions not persisted, conversation history lost on new chat
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailability - external ACP agent history/session management completely broken. Users lose all conversation history permanently. Major pain for anyone using external ACP agents for serious work.

source_issues.title: view agent history does not work for kiro-cli acp

ACP session/list, session/get, session/metadata APIs are not implemented by kiro-cli acp. External agent conversation history is permanently lost.

signals.topic: Terminal tab switch keyboard shortcut doesn't transfer keyboard focus
signals.summary: Ctrl+Tab switches terminal tab visually but focus stays on previous tab
signals.review_reason: Clear UX degradation - keyboard shortcut for terminal tab switching is broken, forcing users to use mouse to interact with newly switched terminal tabs. Breaks core keyboard-driven workflow.

source_issues.title: Switching terminal tabs using keyboard does not change focus
source_issues.evidence: Using Ctrl+Tab to switch to another terminal tab visually switches the view but typing does not work - focus remains on the previous terminal. User must click with mouse to restore focus. Forces mouse usage for terminal workflow.
